_readme: Access + facts cache for the book-log / book-suggest skills. Machine-maintained, fully regenerable — delete any entry and the next run re-derives it. Keeps book-recommendations.md from carrying link-laden Access cells that go stale silently (the Mistborn 2026-08-26 lesson). AUTHORITATIVE for access: when this file and book-recommendations.md disagree, this file wins and the notes get fixed.
_supersededProfileRev: Was a single date, bumped on any rule change, which invalidated every cached judgement at once. Replaced 2026-08-26 by per-dependency counters in book-revs.json: a rule change now invalidates only the estimates that recorded that rule as a dep, and /book-log recomputes exactly those. This file holds dated facts about the world, invalidated by time passing, not by a rule moving. The one exception is the `occultCheck` blocks, which are judgements kept here for their provenance; they stay valid because axis:occult is a mandatory dep on every line of book-estimates.jsonl, so a change to the occult rule re-examines every book regardless.

_ttlDays._note: enAudio.verified means the *search* need not be redone for 30 days, but every link must still be liveness-checked before it is handed to the reader. enAudio.none is deliberately short: Mistborn's 'none' went stale in 4 days.

_states: verified | eloan (the library holds it only as an e-loan, fond 'eKnihy a eAudio' - a real route, screened like any other, but the viewer hides these by default; reader 2026-10-24) | none | doubtful (a route exists but is abridged, AI-narrated or below ~60% of published runtime) | unchecked
_library: `cz.library` absent = Městská knihovna Valašské Meziříčí, the primary. `roznov` = Městská knihovna Rožnov pod Radhoštěm (katalog.knir.cz), used only when the primary has no print copy (reader 2026-10-25); `cz.branches` names the buildings holding a borrowable copy. Written by tools/second-library.py routes.
_enCopy: An English-language print copy at one of the libraries, for a book with no Czech print route there; the English-gems line links it. Roznov holds ~600 English books, Valasske Mezirici ~360. Existence plus a borrowable exemplar is the bar, as for Roznov Czech routes.

books.title: 2061: Odyssey Three
books.author: Arthur C. Clarke
flags: Third novel of the Space Odyssey sequence, after 2001 and 2010; the fourth, 3001, is also in this catalogue (Laser-books 2012).
The recycled text reviewers object to is material reprinted from 2001 and 2010, some of it verbatim.
English original 2061: Odyssey Three, 1987.
Czech edition trans. Zdenek Volny, Laser-books 2012.

books.title: 3001: The Final Odyssey
books.author: Arthur C. Clarke
flags: Fourth novel of the Space Odyssey sequence, after 2001, 2010 and 2061; 2061 is also in this catalogue (Laser-books 2012).
The library annotation says Poole was murdered by a computer - that is the events of the first book, not a mystery plot, so the detective filter does not apply.
English original 3001: The Final Odyssey, 1997.

books.title: A Doggie and a Pussycat
books.author: written and drawn by Josef Čapek

books.title: Forward the Foundation
books.author: Isaac Asimov
flags: Asimov's last novel, published posthumously in 1993; second in internal chronology, after Prelude to Foundation (Nadace - předehra).
Four linked novellas plus an epilogue - Eto Demerzel, Cleon I, Dors Venabili, Wanda Seldon - each a decade apart; a fifth was outlined but never written.
Czech print edition: Triton 2014, translated by Daniela Orlando, ISBN 978-80-257-1285-6.
Reviewers note continuity frictions with the original trilogy, which implies Seldon was obscure and unmarried.

books.title: Alcatraz Versus the Evil Librarians
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: Volume 1 of four; the next volume in this catalogue is 'Alcatraz versus legie Zakladatelovych kosti' (Slovart 2023, same translator).
The author's own site places the series in Middle Grade, 5th to 7th grade, published by Scholastic.
The 'occult' signal in the library annotation is a false positive: the magic is an invented system of Oculator lenses and inherited Smedry Talents, not real-world occultism, and no ritual is enacted.
318 pages, illustrated by Hayley Lazo. A second catalogue record for the same title exists (5fe25a7a-1253-4e06-9c53-79d17e0e5fa3) with no publisher, year or holdings data.

books.title: The Scrivener's Bones
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: Volume 2 of four; the preceding volume in this catalogue is 'Alcatraz versus dabelsti knihovnici' (Slovart 2023, same translator).
The author's own site places the series in Middle Grade, 5th to 7th grade, published by Scholastic.
Invented magic only (Oculator lenses, Smedry Talents); no real-world occult practice is enacted.
332 pages, illustrated by Hayley Lazo.
The Collins decline cited in `why` is Catching Fire, the second Hunger Games volume, 89 to 83.

books.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland / Through the Looking-Glass
books.czTitle: Alenka v kraji divů a za zrcadlem
books.author: Lewis Carroll

cz.note: Both books in one volume. A 1994 Hynek bilingual edition is also held; the Fletna 2018 record is a different author's retelling.

books.occultCheck: Pass. Dream-logic nonsense; nothing operated or invoked.

enAudio.note: Public domain; confirmed against the LibriVox API on 2026-08-27.

books.title: Alma a Svet obrazu
books.author: Lucie Paulova
flags: Illustrated by Katerina Cupova.
Reader reception explicitly wants a sequel, suggesting this may become a series, though no second volume was found.

cz.translator: Jitka Zehnalová, Bob Hýsek a Jan Válek

books.title: Amelia Fang and the Unicorn Lords
books.author: Laura Ellen Andersonová
flags: Part of a 7-book illustrated chapter-book series (Amelia Fang) aimed at roughly ages 6-10; invented gothic-monster fantasy world (Nocturnia), not drawn from real-world occultism.

prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: Amari and the Night Brothers
books.author: B.B. Alston
flags: Investigation-shaped subplot (finding the missing brother); the reader's core arc is belonging/found-family rather than a whodunit.
First of a planned longer middle-grade series (Supernatural Investigations).

books.title: Amari and the Great Game
books.author: B.B. Alston
flags: Second book in the Supernatural Investigations series; continues directly from Amari and the Night Brothers.

books.title: American War
books.author: Omar El Akkad
flags: Narrator's identity is withheld until roughly two-thirds through the book.

books.title: The Gods Themselves
books.author: Isaac Asimov
flags: Won both the Hugo and the Nebula for best novel (1972-73).
Three parts titled from a line of Schiller - Against Stupidity, The Gods Themselves, Contend in Vain? - with separate casts; the second is set entirely in the parallel universe.
Czech print edition: Argo 2014, translated by Viola Somogyi and Zdeněk Lyčka, ISBN 978-80-7387-781-1.
The exact opening scene of part one could not be sourced, only that it starts from the discovery of the Pump and the physicist's objection to it.

books.title: Anna na krku a jine povidky
books.author: Anton Pavlovič Čechov

cz.translator: Jaroslav Hulák, Emanuel Frynta, Zdeňka Psůtková

books.czTitle: Anna na krku a jiné povídky
flags: Selected from the Russian by Jaroslav Hulak; translated by Hulak, Emanuel Frynta and Zdenka Psutkova. First edition in this arrangement, Academia 2000, 399 pp.
Source of the texts is the Soviet 11-volume Sobranije socinenij.
No source found gives a story-by-story table of contents; the count of forty-seven pieces comes from a user-contributed database field.
Sources disagree on the ISBN check digit (80-200-0275-5 vs 80-200-0275-8).

books.title: Anne of Green Gables
books.author: Lucy Maud Montgomery

cz.note: Ilustrovala Zdenka Krejcova. Five print editions held. The library carries the whole eight-volume run plus the three Emily books.

books.occultCheck: Pass.

enAudio.note: Public domain; confirmed against the LibriVox API on 2026-08-27.

books.title: An Anthropologist on Mars
books.author: Oliver Sacks
flags: Czech edition access route is unchecked in the catalogue (no recordId yet).

books.title: Shards of Earth
books.author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
flags: The catalogue titles this record by the series name Architekti světů; the volume is Střepy Země. Volumes 2 (Oči prázdnoty) and 3 (Vládci nestvůrnosti) are in Czech print (Planeta9/Triton 2024) but neither library was found to hold them (2026-10-29).

books.title: Armenska genocida: priciny, prubeh a osobni svedectvi udalosti z let 1915-1922
books.author: Marek Jandak

books.title: Arthur and the Golden Rope
books.author: Joe Todd-Stanton
flags: First book in the 'Brownstone's Mythical Collection' series; a 56-page illustrated picture book that received a starred Kirkus review, recommended age roughly 5-9.

books.title: The Atlas Six
books.author: Olivie Blake
flags: Book 1 of a trilogy (The Atlas Six, The Atlas Paradox, The Atlas Complex).

books.title: Automat svet
books.author: Bohumil Hrabal
flags: A compilation, not an original cycle: the stories are drawn from Perlicka na dne and Pabitele, and story-to-collection attributions differ between Czech editions.
Only the 1966 Mlada fronta printing was found in print in this catalogue; a Popron audiobook of Pabitele and a Supraphon audio selection are also held and are audio, not print.
The hanged body in the title story is a scene-setting fact, not an investigation - no detective plot follows it.

books.title: Fables
books.author: Jean de La Fontaine
flags: Verified Czech route is a 1959 SNKLHU printing, distinct from the 'for the youngest readers' Junior edition (2007/2008) the catalogue annotation appears to describe; abridgement level of the SNKLHU printing was not established.

books.title: Beowulf: A New Telling
books.author: Robert Nye
flags: Occult status not examined -- exited at C-low before Gate 5. The epic includes pagan gods and fate/wyrd themes but no on-page witchcraft or divination was confirmed either way.

books.title: The Cement Garden
books.author: Ian McEwan
flags: McEwan's debut, 1978; about 140 pages, short enough to be read as a novella.
Filmed in 1993 (dir. Andrew Birkin).

Chapter-one construction is sourced only from study-guide summaries, not from a review of the opening itself; the single first-person narrator and the father's death at the start are consistent across those sources.
No occult element of any kind was found in the plot sources.

books.title: UnWholly
books.author: Neal Shusterman
flags: Part of the Unwind Dystology, following directly on the first book.

books.title: UnSouled
books.author: Neal Shusterman
flags: Part of the Unwind Dystology; a review of this entry noted its worldbuilding assumes the reader already knows the system from earlier books in the series rather than re-establishing it on the page.

books.title: Unwind
books.author: Neal Shusterman
flags: Another Czech print edition exists (Knizni klub 2016, same translator Petr Kotrle).
First of four Unwind Dystology books; a later volume is not part of this batch.
Occult status not examined - gate exited at C-low before reaching the occult check.

books.title: Biblicke pribehy pro neverici deti
books.author: Martin Vopěnka
flags: No age limit stated by the publisher, but marketed and reviewed primarily as a children's/YA nonfiction bestseller.
Illustrated by Jiří Votruba; developed with input from a theologian.

books.title: Tales of the Bizarre
books.author: Olga Tokarczuková
flags: No official English translation found as of research; 'Tales of the Bizarre' is the publisher-used working title for the Polish 'Opowiadania bizarne'.

books.title: Crazy Sunday and Other Stories
books.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

cz.translator: Vlasta Dvorackova, Alena Jindrova-Spilarova, Lubomir Doruzka

flags: The catalogue separately holds a simplified bilingual edition of 'The Curious Case of Benjamin Button' alone (Computer Press, 2010).

books.title: Angles of Attack
books.author: Marko Kloos
flags: Volume 3 of the Czech series 'Prvni linie' (8 volumes held in this catalogue); original title Angles of Attack (2015). Czech translation by Jakub Marik.
The whole series is one continuous first-person narrative told by the same narrator, Andrew Grayson, in present tense.
Follows the events of Evakuace (Lines of Departure) directly; 285 pages.

books.title: Labyrinth of Reflections
books.author: Sergei Lukyanenko
flags: First book of Lukyanenko's Labyrinth trilogy.

books.title: Orders of Battle
books.author: Marko Kloos
flags: Volume 7 of the Czech series 'Prvni linie' (8 volumes held in this catalogue); original title Orders of Battle (2020). Czech translation by Jakub Marik.
The whole series is one continuous first-person narrative told by the same narrator, Andrew Grayson, in present tense.
Reads on from Protiuder (Points of Impact); 269 pages.
A reviewer notes this instalment opens a new story arc and recaps enough that it can be read cold, and that it ends on a cliffhanger continued in Posledni hlidka (Centers of Gravity).

books.title: The Obelisk Gate
books.author: N. K. Jemisinová
flags: Second of the Broken Earth trilogy, after The Fifth Season (Czech: Pata rocni doba) and before The Stone Sky; the preceding novel opens on three separate timelines whose connection is withheld, which is the reader's own hard filter and would have to be read first.
Won the Hugo Award for Best Novel, as the preceding novel did.
Reviewers report the book withholds a great deal - Guardian allegiances and stone-eater motives are left unresolved for the final volume.

books.title: The Gates of Athens
books.author: Conn Iggulden
flags: First of the Athenian sequence; Protector continues it directly, and Lion and Empire follow the next generation of Athenians.
Reviews disagree on whether the book carries three, four or five viewpoint characters; one counts five introduced at Marathon.

A blog review refers to the Delphic oracle prophesying Leonidas' fate as appearing in the book. No source found describing animal sacrifice, omen-reading or a priestess officiating in a scene, so the occult question is unresolved.
Czech edition Vysehrad 2024, 451 pages, ISBN 978-80-7601-934-8, translated by Ivan Rycovsky.
Some publisher marketing copy wrongly describes the book as covering the Athens-Sparta conflict; the novel is about the Persian wars.
OCCULT UNRESOLVED after the 2026-08-26 ruling. Needs a text check: the Delphic oracle prophesying Leonidas' fate - enacted in a scene, or reported?

books.title: The Brothers Lionheart
books.author: Astrid Lindgren

cz.note: Prelozila Jarka Vrbova. Also Albatros 2013. About 151 pages.

enAudio.note: Only chapters 1-3 found, 36 min of a roughly 4h30m reading. Partial, not a route.

books.occultCheck: Pass. Nangijala is an afterlife, not a practice: nobody invokes, prays to or operates anything.
flags: Ends with the brothers choosing death; that is the point of the book, not a twist.

books.title: Futu.re
books.author: Dmitry Glukhovsky
flags: Content-warning listings (Internet Archive, StoryGraph) flag graphic violence, explicit sexual content and hate speech; some reviewers read the misogyny as integral to a bleak dystopian critique, others as gratuitous.
Marketed with a 'worthy successor to 1984 and Brave New World' blurb; reception is considerably more mixed than that framing suggests.

books.title: Byla jsem šťastná
books.author: Jarmila Novotná
flags: The catalogue also holds a 1991 first printing and a 2010 audio edition for the visually impaired.

books.title: Bylo nás pět
books.author: Karel Poláček

cz.note: Ilustrovala Helena Zmatlikova. Eight print editions held, 1954-2023; Supraphon 2001 is audio. Czech original.
cz.linkCheck: Record repointed by hand 2026-08-27: fetch-library.py had matched an older or superseded printing of the same work.

enAudio.note: Czech original; no English reading sought.

books.occultCheck: Pass. Realist comic novel.

books.title: Once Upon a Time
books.author: Božena Němcová
flags: Signals field flagged childrens; annotation confirms simplified language for age 4+.

books.title: Carmen - The Real Life of Hana Hegerova
books.author: Tomas Padevet

cz.note: Held only as a library e-loan (eReading), no print copy. Until 2026-10-24 the route read this e-loan record as print.

books.title: Line
books.author: Rjú Murakami
flags: Japanese original title (Line), 1998; some Czech databases transliterate it as Rain, which is the same title.
Not related to Haruki Murakami.
Argo also publishes V polevce miso, Piercing and Nekonecna, temer pruzracna modr by the same author.
Czech critics describe it variously as a fragmentary novella and as near-standalone linked stories; the form field says novel because that is how it is published.
Opening structure inferred from publisher copy and reader reviews - no source describes the first chapter directly.

books.title: Cas malin prezralych
books.author: Marcela Mlynarova
flags: Catalogue subject terms: povidky, autobiograficky, humoristicky. Illustrated by Tereza Budilova.
Published 2026, so no reviews beyond publisher copy were found; the form is established from the catalogue record's contents list and subject terms.
The catalogue holds around twenty further titles by this author, including audiobook editions from Tembr.

books.title: Waiting to Be Arrested at Night
books.czTitle: Čekám, až si pro mě v noci přijdou
books.author: Tahir Hamut Izgil

books.title: Red Dwarf: Infinity Welcomes Careful Drivers
books.author: Rob Grant et Doug Naylor (Grant Naylor)

books.title: Droga donikad (Road to Nowhere)
books.author: Józef Mackiewicz
flags: First part of a war-era dilogy; a second volume exists.

One reader review (Databaze knih) found the opening 90 pages hard to connect with and called it schematic; most other reviews found the same material gripping -- reception is not unanimous on the opening.

books.title: Children of Time
books.author: Adrian Tchaikovsky

enAudio.note: All three query forms run (full / part 1 / narrator). Every hit a 0-2 min stub across six channels; 991 min published. Czech print is the only route.

books.provenance: Found by catalogue discovery sweep 2026-08-26, not by name lookup.

books.title: The Paul Street Boys
books.author: Ferenc Molnár

cz.note: Prelozil Ladislav Hradsky, ilustroval Karoly Reich. Sole holding, 159 pages.

books.occultCheck: Pass. Realist novel, nothing supernatural.

books.title: The Boy on the Bridge
books.author: M. R. Carey
books.series: The Girl with All the Gifts
flags: Prequel to The Girl with All the Gifts, set 10 years earlier; readable as a standalone.
Read after Všemi dary obdarovaná: the epilogue, set years later, reportedly gives away that novel's ending.

books.title: The Boy in the Striped Pyjamas
books.author: John Boyne

cz.note: Prelozila Jarka Stuchlikova. Also Slovart 2020. The K. E. Macan 2019 record is audio for the blind.

books.occultCheck: Pass. Historical fiction.
flags: Recorded, not proposed - see the estimate. Kept so the title stops resurfacing in every children's sweep.

books.title: The Emperor of Gladness
books.author: Ocean Vuong
flags: 2025 English release, 2026 Czech translation; too recent for a long critical track record.

books.title: Pure
books.author: Julianna Baggott
flags: First book of a trilogy (Pure, Fuse, Burn).

books.title: The Neil Gaiman Reader
books.author: Neil Gaiman
flags: Includes short excerpts from five novels alongside near fifty stories, so some content is fragmentary rather than complete works.
Selections were chosen by reader vote rather than by the author or an outside editor.

books.title: The City and Its Uncertain Walls
books.author: Haruki Murakami

cz.note: catalogue holds only a foreign-language edition (Vintage 2025)

books.title: Bridge of Clay
books.author: Markus Zusak
flags: Zusak's first novel since The Book Thief, a 13-year gap; several reviewers note it inevitably suffers by comparison to that earlier, more acclaimed book.
Narrated by the eldest brother, Matthew, rather than by Clay himself; reviewers describe the time-jumping structure as easy to follow despite starting near the end.

books.title: Conan
books.author: Robert Ervin Howard
flags: The catalogue also holds a duplicate print listing: AFSF 1997, same translators (Jan Kantůrek a Bedřich Možucha).

books.title: Cytonic
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: Volume 3 of the Skyward series; earlier volumes in this catalogue are 'Vzhuru k obloze' (Talpress 2019) and 'Vyhled na hvezdy' (Talpress 2020), same translator.
Widely ranked the weakest instalment of its series by reviewers; the split is roughly 3/5 against 4/5, not a consensus panning.
I did not find a source describing the first chapter specifically, so the opening structure is inferred from the series' established single-POV narration - hence medium confidence.

books.title: The Dalai Lama's Cat and the Claw of Attraction
books.author: David Michie
flags: Sixth book in an ongoing series; other Czech print/audio editions of this and earlier volumes exist (Synergie 2013 print, Synergie 2015 audio).

books.title: The Queen's Gambit
books.author: Walter Tevis
flags: Source for the 2020 Netflix adaptation; multiple reviewers say the novel has more depth than the show.

books.title: The Gift of the Magi
books.author: O. Henry
flags: This 2024 Mladá fronta edition is a single 40-page illustrated printing of the one story, not a collection; reader reviews note the text feels abridged relative to other translations, and its childlike illustration style is aimed at 12+ despite the picture-book appearance.

cz.note: Print in both 2013 (váz.) and 2014 (brož.); sequels Hledání modré, Posel v temném lese, Syn also held.

cz.editionWarning: The 2025 Tympanum record is audio-only, not print.

books.title: Diamonds of the Night
books.author: Arnošt Lustig
flags: Eighth Czech edition (Mlada fronta 2011, 186 pages); first published 1958.
Filmed in 1964 by Jan Nemec as 'Demanty noci', with the author co-writing the screenplay.
Contents: Sousto, Druhe kolo, Bily, Starci a smrt, Zacatek a konec, Michael a druhy s dykou, Tma nema stin, Chlapec u okna, Cerny lev.
The story 'Tma nema stin' was later expanded and also exists as a separate book.

books.title: Day
books.author: Michael Cunningham
flags: First published in the US by Random House in November 2023; the 2024 dates belong to the UK and Czech editions.
Czech print route is Odeon 2024, translated by Veronika Volhejnova.

books.title: A Day of Fallen Night
books.author: Samantha Shannon
flags: Companion volume: Prevorstvi u pomerancovniku (Host 2020, translated by Lenka Kapsova, record 03c35a25-27be-46ab-93c1-9ae15c07b178) is set centuries later in the same world; either can be read first.
Different Czech translator from the author's other Host titles.
868 pages; four viewpoints on four continents, and the fourth is reported to arrive as a full viewpoint later than the other three.
Sources conflict on whether all four viewpoints appear inside part one or the fourth begins in part two.
OCCULT UNRESOLVED after the 2026-08-26 ruling. Needs a text check: prayer to the book's invented gods - is a prayer or offering shown in a scene?

books.title: Children of Ruin
books.author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
flags: A sequel; reviewers state it is not a standalone and should not be read first. The preceding volume is available in Czech as Deti casu (Triton 2018, translated by Zdenek Uhercik, record b9268894-17c1-4571-8385-7f88f241148e).
One strand turns to body horror; not recommended by reviewers for readers avoiding horror.
Past sections are third-person past tense, present sections third-person present tense.
Other Tchaikovsky titles in this catalogue: Klec dusi (Planeta9 2020), Architekti svetu (Planeta9/Triton 2022), Rubas (Planeta9 2026).

books.title: Momo
books.author: Michael Ende

cz.note: The 2005 Albatros record is the full novel. The 2025 Albatros record titled just Devcatko Momo is a retelling - prevypravel Uwe-Michael Gutzschhahn - so borrow the 2005 one.

enAudio.note: Only chapter-by-chapter uploads on a single channel (d8TyXafHyqc onward); completeness not verified, so not linked as a route.

books.occultCheck: Pass. Master Hora and the hour-lilies are numinous rather than operated - nothing is invoked, learned or performed.
flags: Same author as Nekonecny pribeh; the two are independent.

books.title: Chains of Command
books.author: Marko Kloos
flags: Volume 4 of the Czech series 'Prvni linie' (8 volumes held in this catalogue); original title Chains of Command (2016). Czech translation by Jakub Marik.
The whole series is one continuous first-person narrative told by the same narrator, Andrew Grayson, in present tense.
Reads on from Blokada (Angles of Attack); 318 pages.
Two reviewers call this the weakest instalment so far, citing pacing and thin character development.

excluded.why: Divinities are invented so the source test passes, but miracles work as rituals that Shara and Sigrud learn and perform on the page. Hard filter, so dropped rather than caveated. Evidence is fan-wiki/review level, not authorial — revisit only if the reader disputes it.

books.title: Girl, Woman, Other
books.author: Bernardine Evaristo
flags: Booker Prize co-winner 2019 (with Margaret Atwood's The Testaments).
Occult status not examined -- not applicable to this contemporary realist novel, no fantastical elements present in any summary found.

books.title: Les pierres sauvages
books.author: Fernand Pouillon
flags: The Czech edition's route is currently unchecked (no recordId), unlike the other books in this batch.

books.title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
books.author: Mark Twain

cz.note: Full translation. Also Mlada fronta 1965. Avoid the Grada 2010 record and the INFOA 2014 one - Grada publishes graphic adaptations and INFOA a graded reader; the Supraphon records are audio.

books.occultCheck: Pass. Jim's superstitions are described as beliefs held by a character, never enacted as an efficacious rite.

enAudio.note: Public domain; confirmed against the LibriVox API on 2026-08-27.

books.title: Perfect
books.author: Cecelia Ahern
flags: Second book of a duology; the catalogue's 'King Cool' series label is a Czech publisher imprint, not the original duology name.

prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: Giu nella valle
books.author: Paolo Cognetti
flags: 123 pages, translated by Sara Rodova; original Italian Giu nella valle, Einaudi 2023.
Luigi is a forest policeman and one strand follows the shooting of dogs along the Sesia - an investigation-shaped subplot, not the engine of the book, which is the inheritance quarrel.
I could not source how chapter 1 opens or how many threads are running by the end of it; the opening axis is therefore unverified.
Italian reception is sharply divided, including at least one outright negative review.

books.title: The Letter for the King
books.author: Tonke Dragt

cz.note: Prelozila Jana Irmannova-Pellarova. 456 pages.

books.occultCheck: Pass. No magic in it at all - a chivalric adventure in an invented but mundane kingdom.
flags: Sequel also held: Tajemstvi Divokeho hvozdu (Albatros 2025, 509 pages), unassessed.

books.title: Love Letters to the Dead
books.author: Ava Dellaira
flags: Widely compared by reviewers to The Perks of Being a Wallflower.

books.title: Nicht normal aber das richtig gut
books.author: Denise Linkeová

books.title: The Dragon's Path
books.author: Daniel Abraham

enAudio.note: Only a publisher sample found.

books.provenance: Exhaustive genre screen 2026-08-26. Abraham is half of James S. A. Corey.

books.title: Draci mesto
books.author: Petra Machova
flags: axis:occult not examined - C-low exit happens before gate 5 in the ladder's cost order; the lizard-people magic/lore appears to be invented rather than drawn from real-world occult practice, for what that is worth.

books.title: Burn
books.author: Patrick Ness
flags: Standalone; unconnected to the author's Chaos Walking books.
Czech edition translated by Hana Březáková (Slovart 2023).
Four perspectives are used - Sarah, the dragon Kazimir, the assassin Malcolm, and the Goddess - and switches sometimes occur mid-chapter.
Contains a same-sex relationship in the assassin's storyline, and depicts period racism against Black and Japanese American characters.
The cult's deity is an invented dragon goddess; no real-world pantheon or occult practice is involved.
About halfway through, the story moves into a parallel universe in which dragons never existed.
OCCULT UNRESOLVED after the 2026-08-26 ruling. Needs a text check: one of four POVs is a goddess - is she petitioned in a scene?

books.title: Second Foundation
books.author: Isaac Asimov

No Czech-only print edition of this title was found in this catalogue.

Reviewers note eerie parallels to COVID-19 despite the book predating the pandemic by two years.
Reviewers describe the premise as derivative, comparing it to Jurassic Park and Rise of the Planet of the Apes.

books.title: The Incredible and Sad Tale of Innocent Eréndira and Her Heartless Grandmother
books.author: Gabriel García Márquez

flags: The Czech edition is a seven-story collection headed by this title (V Praze : Odeon, 2008, přel. Blanka Stárková) - the other six stories are untouched by this assessment.
Content note: the first sexual encounter is an explicit rape depicted as violent assault, not eroticized - intense despite being seriously (not crudely) handled.

No real-world occult ritual - divination, witchcraft, séance, or prayer/sacrifice to a real deity - was found enacted on the page across multiple plot summaries, reviews, and academic sources. The magical-realism touches (diamonds grown inside oranges, telepathic summoning across the desert, the ghosts of the dead Amadises) are invented fabulist dressing, not real-world occult practice.

books.title: Lines of Departure
books.author: Marko Kloos
flags: Volume 2 of the Czech series 'Prvni linie' (8 volumes held in this catalogue); original title Lines of Departure (2014). Czech translation by Jakub Marik.

Reads on from Smlouva na zivot (Terms of Enlistment); 269 pages.
A full-series reviewer describes this volume as containing an element of wheelspinning.

books.title: Exordia

books.title: The Farm

books.title: Flashforward

books.title: The Photographer of Mauthausen

Interleaves the protagonist's narration with entries from her mother's journal; it is not a multi-POV novel in the usual sense.
The English editions carry black-and-white illustrations by Manuel Šumberac; whether the Czech edition reproduces them was not verified.
Sources disagree on the protagonist's stated age - some say fourteen, the UK publisher says sixteen.

books.title: The Chaperone

books.title: A Gentleman in Moscow

Chapter intervals widen from days to years after the 1922 sentencing and then contract again; this accordion structure is reported by a secondary source and not confirmed against an author interview.

books.title: The Gernsback Continuum

cz.note: Czech original, no translation involved. Also held: Hotýlek (Host 2015, 2019) and Tiché roky (Host 2019). The 2019 'Knihovna a tiskárna pro nevidomé K. E. Macana' records are NOT general-loan print.

Graded for roughly ages 11-14 (grades 5-8 by one source, 5-12 by another); about 47,900 words, Lexile 680L.

One Czech print edition found (Baronet 2010, trans. Ivana Nuhlickova).

Reader content-warning sources report torture and off-page sexual violence across the later volumes.
OCCULT UNRESOLVED after the 2026-08-26 ruling. Needs a text check: Hebrew-derived pantheon - Source question, plus is any rite shown in a scene?

A Tembr audiobook of the same Senkyrik translation, read by Gustav Hasek, also exists (2023) - not the route used for this promotion.
The English original title is Lessons, not The Hours; czTitle 'Hodiny' is a coincidental match with the more famous Cunningham book of the same Czech name.

Czech print, ISBN 978-80-7491-522-2.

Occult question not verified story by story across seventy stories. Titles in the selection such as Carodejne jaro and Strycek Einar turn on invented supernatural beings rather than on sourced ritual, but no source was found confirming that no piece enacts a real-world rite on the page.
Opening structure is per story rather than per book; the contents listing was used to establish that each piece starts from a single concrete situation.
OCCULT UNRESOLVED after the 2026-08-26 ruling. Needs a text check: seventy stories, not verified one by one; does any piece enact a real-world rite?

books.title: Kluby poezie

flags: The two source texts are Nezny barbar and Prilis hlucna samota; this is not a complete edition of either, and it does not contain Tanecni hodiny pro starsi a pokrocile despite the two titles often sitting side by side in catalogues.

Heavily marked by censorship and self-censorship: references to the normalisation present, plus philosophical, erotic and grotesque passages, were removed, and the rhythmic repetition principle weakened. The uncut Prilis hlucna samota appeared only later (Odeon 1989; Sebrane spisy 1994).
Form is recorded as novella because the montage reads as one continuous interleaved text, but it is strictly an assembled compilation of excerpts rather than a work of that form.
A partial text is available as a PDF from the Municipal Library of Prague.

books.title: The Graveyard Book

books.title: The King's Blood

Chapter-one structure was not sourced for this individual volume; the rotating four-to-five viewpoint pattern (Cithrin, Geder, Marcus, Clara, plus Dawson early on) is sourced at series level.

SKIP THOSE TWO and the remaining six are the strongest axis match in the catalogue. The estimate assumes he does; if he reads straight through, treat it as a low-50s book.
Neither story appears in Vydech, which is unaffected and is the volume to propose first.

books.title: Anděl
books.author: Denisa Tatíčková
flags: Roughly 160 pages; one retailer credits a co-author, Drahomir Rybnicek, and dates the edition 2011.

books.title: Atlantis
books.author: Greg Donegan
flags: Greg Donegan is a pen name of Bob Mayer, who also wrote later volumes as Robert Doherty.
Book one of six; the sequels are Bermuda Triangle, Devil's Sea, Atlantis Gate, Assault on Atlantis and Battle for Atlantis.

books.title: Azincourt
books.author: Bernard Cornwell
flags: Published in the United States as Agincourt.
The protagonist hears the voices of Saints Crispin and Crispinian, which several reviewers treat as an unexplained supernatural device used to extract him from danger.
The author's Saxon Stories sequence is excluded on the occult filter; this is an unrelated standalone.

books.title: Benrok
books.author: Helena Bernardová
flags: Retailer listings give the full title as Benrok: Zavrzene mesto and pitch it at readers of Paolini's Inheritance Cycle.
An English edition exists as Benrok: The Forsaken City.

books.title: The White Pearl
books.author: Kate Furnivallová
flags: The catalogue annotation is a first-act summary only; the bulk of the novel takes place at sea.
The protagonist's earlier lover was a Japanese man whose death she is implicated in; sources disagree on whether it was suicide or an accident during a struggle.
The dying woman's curse and the servant girl's attempt to carry it out is a plot thread; whether anything supernatural is enacted was not investigated.

books.title: The Fist of God
books.author: Frederick Forsyth
flags: About 592 pages; reportedly the first major popular novel dealing entirely with the 1990-91 Gulf War.
Built on a fictionalised retelling of the real Iraqi Project Babylon supergun.
The narrative alternates between Allied command, Saddam's war cabinet, Allied pilots and the agent in Baghdad; the agent Mike Martin also appears in a later Forsyth novel.

books.title: Go as a River
books.author: Shelley Read
flags: Based on the real destruction of Iola, Colorado, now under the Blue Mesa Reservoir.
The author's debut novel (2023).

books.title: Carovenik
books.author: Marie Rejfova
flags: First of a series; the sequel is Sestra smrt, in which the two leads return to our world.
Goodreads rating 3.33 from a small sample; Czech readers' comments split between readable and first-novel rough.

books.title: Black Cake
books.author: Charmaine Wilkerson
flags: A murder suspicion and a missing child drive the plot, but the book is a family saga rather than a detective novel.
The author's debut novel (2022).

books.title: The Course of Honour
books.author: Lindsey Davisová
flags: Standalone. Not part of the author's Falco or Flavia Albia investigator series - written before them, published 1997 after those made her name. The already-excluded detective titles by this author (Nepritel v dome, Mrtvola v lazni, Videt Delfy a zemrit) are a different series with different leads.
Czech edition BB/art 2013, transl. Zdenek Hron; original title The Course of Honour.
Historically and in the novel, Roman law barred a senator from marrying a freedwoman; that prohibition, not adultery, is the obstacle the plot turns on.

books.title: Cesta pouští
books.author: Ota B. Kraus
flags: Written in English in the 1980s and first published in Czech only in 2014 (Akropolis, transl. Alice Marxova) - unlike the author's other books, which he translated himself.
Publisher and review copy mention a mysterious farm where both Germans and witches figure; nothing further established.
Other works by the same author in Czech: Zeme bez Boha, Vitr z hor, Muj bratr dym, Vepri ve pri, Obchodnik se sny.
The English original's title was not established; the Czech edition is a translation from English by Alice Marxova.

books.title: Cestovatelská krev
books.author: Tereza Kučírková
flags: 256 pages; reviewed in the Czech SF magazine XB-1, issue 2019/11.
Print run appears sold out at most Czech retailers.

books.title: Hasidic Tales of the Holocaust
books.author: Yaffa Eliach
flags: First published in English by Oxford University Press, 1982.
The collection mixes documented testimony with miracle tales; the historicity of at least one has been contested in the scholarly literature.

books.title: Chrlič
books.author: Vojtěch Otčenášek
flags: 120 pages, illustrated, catalogued as children's fiction; subtitled Boj dobra a zla ve stare Praze.
An e-book edition is dated 2015.

books.title: China: The Novel
books.author: Edward Rutherfurd

Czech translation BB/art 2022, prel. Zdenek Hron.

books.title: Das Erbe der Nibelungen

books.title: The Diplomat's Wife

books.title: The Sea Gate

books.title: Sins of the House of Borgia (originally The Book of Love)

books.title: You Had Me at Hello
books.author: Mhairi McFarlane

Occult status unexamined at this exit.

books.title: Něco úžasného

The supernatural Fogs and Clears are ambient presences; no rite is performed by any character on the page.

books.title: Nightbirds
books.author: Kate J. Armstrong
flags: First of a series; a second volume exists.
Marketed as young adult; the clients-by-night framing sits close to a courtesan setting without the plot being sexual.

books.title: Mathias Sandorf

cz.state on the task line is 'unchecked' and carries no record id.

books.title: Nový věk

Both first circulated in samizdat and in the exile journal Svědectví; this is the first textually revised book edition, with an afterword by Martin Machovec.
One reference work dates Nový věk to the first century rather than the seventeenth; the sources conflict.

books.title: Seed to Dust: A Gardener's Story
books.author: Marc Hamer
flags: Published in the UK as Seed to Dust: A Gardener's Story and in North America as Seed to Dust: Life, Nature, and a Country Garden.

books.title: Ostrov ztracenych snu

books.title: Personal Recollections of Joan of Arc
books.author: Mark Twain

books.title: Po stopach ztraceneho syna
books.author: Petr Hugo Slik

The catalogue record gives no verified Czech print holding (cz.state unchecked).

books.title: Pohadka z hnizda

flags: Published in the Cteni pro prvnacky (Reading for First-Graders) edition - illustrated, for children just starting to read.

The catalogue record gives no verified Czech print holding (cz.state unchecked).

books.title: Popletene pocitani

The catalogue record gives no verified Czech print holding (cz.state unchecked).

books.title: The First Time
books.author: Joy Fielding
flags: The task line named a separate already-excluded standalone by this author, Spatna dcera, on a detective filter; the two books share no series and no characters.

books.title: Battle Flag

books.title: The Midnight Rose

flags: Reviewers describe the heroine as having second sight and the book as carrying a ghost-story strand; that content was not examined at this exit.

books.title: Rebel

books.title: Révi a Město snů
books.author: Veronika Hurdová

books.title: Sesterstvo a sila moci

Polish original 1923 (one source gives 1922); a 2004 English edition runs 330 pages.
A sequel, Krol Macius na wyspie bezludnej (King Matt on a Desert Island), continues from the exile this book ends in and restores him and democracy to his country.
Beware adaptation-contaminated summaries: the 2002-2006 animated series resolves the story happily, unlike the book.
The reading that the book carries an anti-racism thread via Matt's love for an African princess comes from a single pop-culture blog, not a scholarly source.

No source consulted described any magic, seance or rite in the text; the fairy-tale form here is political allegory, so the occult question is inferred from absence rather than positively sourced - hence medium confidence.

books.author: Knauerová, Marta
flags: Czech route unverified: cz.state is "unchecked", so publisher (CPress) and year (2022) are known but the catalogue record was not confirmed.
First edition CPress 2021 (edice Vánoční knížky); the 2022 printing is the second edition and a third followed in 2025.
208 pages, hardback, illustrated by Atila Vörös; some retailers add Jana Drnková as a co-author, which is unconfirmed.
Czech original, no translation involved.

books.title: Vombat Jirka je statecny
books.author: Eva Papoušková
flags: A sequel: the first book is 'Vombat Jirka' (Mladá fronta 2016) and a further title 'Vombat Jirka zachraňuje' exists; all illustrated by Galina Miklínová.
Reception of the first book is mixed - praised as first-reading material, criticised by one reader for how the parents get their way.
Czech route not verified against the catalogue record (cz.state unchecked).

books.title: Selityspakki
books.author: Onkeli, Kreetta
flags: Finnish original Selityspakki; Czech translation by Martina Simova, illustrations by Ninka Reittu-Kuurila, imprint Drobek, 144 pp.
Czech route unverified - cz.state is 'unchecked': publisher and year known, catalogue record not confirmed.

books.title: Zachumlej se, pohádka začíná
books.author: Rusnáková, Olga
flags: Pointa, 2023, 112 pp, illustrated by Dagmar Chladkova, age 4+; an e-book and a multi-voice Czech audiobook also exist.
Czech route unverified - cz.state is 'unchecked': publisher and year known, catalogue record not confirmed.

books.title: Ztracený na Nevděku
books.author: Petr Hugo Šlik
flags: Czech route unverified: cz.state is 'unchecked', no catalogue record was confirmed, and publisher and year are copied from the task line (Albatros 2021).
128 pages, illustrated by Petr Morkes; presented by Albatros as following the author's Dobrodruzstvi z Klarova series, but with a new setting and lead.
A bonus chapter is not printed in the book - readers have to find it at the ruins of Nevdek castle.
One reader complains the collapsed-tunnel ending repeats that of the author's Tajemstvi jeskyne pokladu.

books.title: Isabela a zelené šelmy
books.author: Peroutková, Ivana
flags: Czech route unverified: cz.state is "unchecked", so publisher (Albatros) and year (2025) are known but the catalogue record was not confirmed; a 2025 release is consistent with an Albatros club circular of 25 April 2025 but was not confirmed from a primary record.
Fourth volume of the Isabela series; reading order is Isabela a bílé mraky, Isabela a žluté útesy, Isabela a červené šípky, Isabela a zelené šelmy.
112 pages per an e-book lending record (not confirmed against the publisher). Czech original, no translation involved.
The same author writes the Anička and Valentýnka series.

books.title: Melissa (originally published as George)
books.author: Gino, Alex
flags: Czech route unverified: cz.state is "unchecked", so publisher (Albatros) and year (2023) are known but the catalogue record was not confirmed.
Published in English as George (Scholastic, 2015) and retitled Melissa in 2021; the Czech edition uses the later title.
224 pages; intended readership 8-12. Won the Stonewall Book Award, a Lambda Literary Award and the California Book Award for Juvenile, and appeared on the ALA most-challenged list 2016-2020.

books.title: Nové Boříkovy lapálie
books.author: Steklač, Vojtěch
flags: Czech route unverified: cz.state is "unchecked", so publisher (Albatros) and year (2022) are known but the catalogue record was not confirmed.
The 2022 Albatros printing is the third edition; the book first appeared in 2002 (ISBN 80-00-01079-8), with a further reprint in 2024. 192 pages, from age 9.
A sequel within the Boříkovy lapálie series, which began with Boříkovy lapálie; a collected Velké Boříkovy lapálie also exists.
Czech original, no translation involved.

books.title: Afterland
books.author: Lauren Beukes
flags: Published as Motherland in some markets.
Chapters are labelled by viewpoint character - Cole, Miles or Billie - with interludes filling in the pandemic's backstory.
Features a repentance sect, the Church of All Sorrows, whose induction rite reviewers call harrowing without describing it; the content of that scene could not be established from available sources.
A scholarly review criticises the novel's handling of a transgender character.

books.title: Areston
books.author: Josef Pecinovský
flags: First of a trilogy: Areston, Utek z Arestonu, Vladce Arestonu, plus a companion volume Stavitele Arestonu.
Reviewers report the book does not resolve and pushes the reader into the next volume; questions raised here are reported still open after the trilogy ends.

The catalogue subject tags include inkvizice; I did not establish from sources whether any rite is performed on the page, so axis:occult is asserted clean only on the absence of any mention in two reviews.

books.title: The End of the World Running Club
books.author: Adrian J. Walker
flags: The catalogue records the author as 'Andrian J. Walker'; the name is Adrian J. Walker.
A companion novel from the wife's point of view exists: The End of the World Survivors Club.
Originally self-published in 2014, then Del Rey 2016 and Sourcebooks Landmark 2017.
The first chapter is narrated from the end of the journey and establishes the narrator as unreliable.

books.title: Bitva o ceske zeme
books.author: Jan Kotouč
flags: Volume five of a six-book series (Brokilon 2022); preceded by Nad českými zeměmi slunce nezapadá (2016), Ofenziva českých zemí (2017), V tajné službě Koruny české (2019) and Spojenci českých zemí (2020).
Depends on the preceding volumes for the war situation and the cast, though the annotation re-states the flooded-world premise.
Occult status not examined - the ladder exits before that gate.

books.title: Blackout
books.author: Jan Kovanic
flags: First published 1999; the Epocha printing is a second edition, roughly 232 to 240 pages. Sources disagree on whether that printing is 2011 or 2012; the catalogue record gives 2011.
Written as a companion to Ondrej Neff's novel Tma, for which the author was a test reader. It is a separate book and readers who had not read Tma report no difficulty.
No professional review was located; reception rests on reader comments.

books.title: Centralni imperium: Omega
books.author: Jan Kotouč
flags: The catalogue record carries the series name as the title; this is the second volume of the two-book Centrální impérium: Omega prequel duology (Brokilon 2024), listed elsewhere as Expanzní sektor.
Continues directly from Komanda Omega - the unit, the betrayal and the lead are established there and assumed here.
A prequel to the main Centrální impérium series (Hranice impéria, Císař v exilu, Obránci civilizace, Odkaz Protektorů), where Hila Ebanová appears as empress.
Ratings on the Czech databases rest on very small samples.
No source establishes the chapter-one POV structure.

books.title: Through the Ever Night
books.author: Veronica Rossi
flags: Second part of the trilogy: Pod nekonecnou oblohou, Cesta vecnou noci, Do poklidne modri; the catalogue annotation names the following volume as Do neklidne modri, which is the same book as Do poklidne modri.
Catalogued as publikace pro mladez / americke romany.
Czech edition Knizni klub 2013, translated by Michaela Skultety.
Two novellas exist in the series (Roar and Liv; Brooke), apparently not published in Czech.

prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: Cisar v exilu
books.author: Jan Kotouč
flags: Volume two of the Centrální impérium series (Fantom Print 2019); Hranice impéria precedes it, Obránci civilizace and Odkaz Protektorů follow in 2020.
Continues directly from Hranice impéria - the lead and the political situation are established there and assumed here.
The prequel duology Centrální impérium: Omega (Brokilon 2024) sits earlier in internal chronology.
No source establishes the chapter-one POV count; the preceding volume's opening was criticised as slow and expository rather than confusing.

books.title: Day Zero
books.author: C. Robert Cargill
flags: A prequel to Sea of Rust (2017) in the same setting; it introduces its own lead and premise and reads standalone.
Reviewers note a shift in the last third toward sustained action; one calls the vocabulary level young-adult.

books.title: Děsy první republiky
books.author: Marek Skřipský
flags: Laser (Euromedia Group) 2024, 240 pages, four stories.
Characters from the author's earlier books, Bronsky and Parma, appear in cameo roles; the collection is described as a good entry point to his work.
Sarden.cz carries a full review that was not read; no other professional review was located.

books.title: The Long Way to a Small, Angry Planet
books.author: Becky Chambers
books.czTitle: Dlouha cesta na malou, rozzlobenou planetu
flags: First of the Wayfarers books; later volumes follow different characters.
Third person alternating between most of the crew rather than a single protagonist, despite the jacket copy foregrounding the newcomer.
Reader-compiled content notes: frequent swearing, offscreen and non-explicit sex including interspecies and non-monogamous relationships, drug use, war and grief.

books.title: Dlouhy cerny usvit
books.author: Jiří W. Procházka
flags: Volume 27 of the multi-author Agent John Francis Kovář series (Triton 2012), created by Jiří Walker Procházka and Miroslav Žamboch on the Perry Rhodan / Mark Stone dime-novel model; Procházka wrote about ten of the volumes, Žamboch about fourteen, with Ondřej Neff, Vladimír Šlechta, Karolina Francová and others contributing.
Deep in a long shared-universe run - the Agency EF setting and the lead are established in far earlier volumes.
Occult status not examined - the ladder exits before that gate.

books.title: Into the Still Blue
books.author: Veronica Rossi
flags: Third and final part of the trilogy: Pod nekonecnou oblohou, Cesta vecnou noci, Do poklidne modri; it follows on directly and is not an entry point.
Catalogued as publikace pro mladez / americke romany / vedecko-fantasticke romany.
Czech edition Knizni klub 2014, translated by Michaela Skultety.

prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: Druhá šance
books.author: Adam Pýcha
flags: Debut, 360 pages, Fobos 2021. The author works in the marketing department of Knihy Dobrovsky, of which Fobos is an imprint, and several readers mention heavy promotion in his own Facebook group.
Marketed 'for Stephen King fans', a comparison reviewers reject.
Audiobook edition exists.

books.title: Dune: The Duke of Caladan
books.author: Brian Herbert, Kevin J. Anderson

cz.linkCheck: 2026-10-24 by hand: repointed from 095b78b6-d9a9-4963-8f5c-1fba16c811bb (Baronet 2022, whose annotation is Lady Jessica, i.e. The Lady of Caladan) to the 2021 record whose annotation is Duke Leto, i.e. The Duke of Caladan

flags: Written by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson, not Frank Herbert; the catalogue records it under the bare title Duna, the original is Dune: The Duke of Caladan (2020).
Set immediately before Frank Herbert's Dune and assumes that novel's world; continues into Dune: The Heir of Caladan and Dune: The Lady of Caladan.
The Baronet 2022 record also titled 'Duna' is the third Caladan book, The Lady of Caladan, not another edition of this one.

books.title: Epizody 2084
books.author: Pavel Hénik
flags: Sources disagree on the count: most say twenty stories, one reader review says eighteen plus a bonus story.
The fullest available review is hosted by Knihy Dobrovsky, which is also the publisher.
Czech audiobook read by Petr Gelnar (Kanopa/Dobrovsky).
Named stories include Pravidla konsenzuality, Tridirna zen and Na lovu, described by readers as respectively comic and harsh.

books.title: The Fandom
books.author: Anna Day
flags: First of two; The Fandom Rising follows.
YA. Reviewers report light romance, profanity and several jarring scenes of sexual assault and violence.
Czech edition Baronet 2018, translated by Jirina Starkova.
The author is a clinical psychologist; the in-book franchise came from her own shortlisted manuscript The Gallows Dance.

books.title: The Exiled Fleet
books.author: J.S. Dewes
flags: Second of J.S. Dewes's The Divide trilogy; continues Hlidka na konci vesmiru.
Read in order - reviewers warn that starting here leaves a reader lost.
The English trilogy closes with The Last Sentinel, not yet listed in Czech.

books.title: The Last Watch
books.author: J.S. Dewes
flags: First of J.S. Dewes's The Divide trilogy; the Czech run continues with Flotila zatracenych.
The English trilogy closes with The Last Sentinel, not yet listed in Czech.

books.title: Hranice imperia
books.author: Jan Kotouč
flags: Volume one of the Centrální impérium series (Fantom Print 2019, 384 s.); Císař v exilu follows in 2019, then Obránci civilizace and Odkaz Protektorů in 2020.

A separate prequel duology, Centrální impérium: Omega (Brokilon 2024), precedes this book in internal chronology; at least one reviewer recommends reading Omega first, which is a reader opinion rather than a publisher statement.
Cover carries a promotional blurb attributed to David Weber - retail marketing copy, not independently verified.
No source found that states how many POVs are live by the end of chapter one; the opening is described only as slow and expository, not as confusing.

books.title: Hvezdni honaci
books.author: Jiří W. Procházka
flags: Novel, not a story collection - 336 pages, Triton 2017, published in the Trifid line; the catalogue's genre heading reads 'vědecko-fantastické příběhy', which is a heading rather than a statement of form.
Audiobook read by Jiří Klem.
Reader reception is sharply split, and reviewers repeatedly contrast this novel unfavourably with the author's short fiction.
Occult status not examined - the ladder exits before that gate.

books.title: Hvezdy ceske sci-fi
books.author: editor Ondrej Jires
flags: Contents: Ondrej Neff 'Prazdniny v mezisvete', Vladimir Slechta 'Chcipnout jako pes', Jaroslav Velinsky 'Ghebrthouxwnlck', Jiri Walker Prochazka 'Rudy soumrak', Vilma Kadleckova 'Lunapark Luna'.
Each novella is set inside the author's own existing series, so none is a standalone entry point.
Kadleckova's 'Lunapark Luna' won an Akademie SFFH short-form prize.

books.title: Die Optimierer
books.author: Theresa Hannig
flags: A sequel, Die Unvollkommenen (2019), is set five years later.
Won the Stefan-Luebbe-Preis 2016 and the Seraph 2018 for best debut; German audiobook 2018.
German reviewers place it in a wave with Kling's QualityLand and Zeh's Leere Herzen.

books.title: The Body Snatchers
books.author: Jack Finney
flags: The Body Snatchers, 1955, roughly 190 pages; serialised in Collier's in 1954. Four film adaptations exist (1956, 1978, 1993, 2007) and all end more bleakly than the novel, in which the pods do not win.
The town is Mill Valley in the novel; Santa Mira is the 1956 film's invention.
An investigation-shaped thread runs through it - Bennell working out what is happening - but the payoff is not the identity of a culprit.
Czech edition Dobrovsky 2023 in the Fobos line, translated by Martin Svetlik.

books.title: Kepler62: Hemmeligheten
books.author: Bjørn Sortland, Timo Parvela

cz.translator: s přihlédnutím k finskému překladu) Jitka Jindřišková a Mic

flags: The sixth and closing volume of the Kepler62 series (original Kepler62 - Hemmeligheten / Salaisuus), Czech title Tajemstvi, published by Host; the catalogue records it under the bare series name Kepler62.
The premise, the crew and the narrator are established in the earlier volumes (Pozvanka, Odpocitavani, Prukopnici and the following two) and assumed here; the series should be read in order.
About 190 pages, illustrated by Pasi Pitkanen; catalogued as a publication for children, with an age recommendation of 9+ given for the first volume.
A reviewer singles out the detailed description of the neurotuning process as unpleasant and reports aggression among the children themselves.
The catalogue also holds another print edition: Host 2018.

books.title: Kepler62: The Invitation
books.author: Timo Parvela, Bjorn Sorland
flags: First of six volumes in the Finnish-Norwegian Kepler62 series; each volume ends on a cliffhanger.
Original book 1 title The Invitation / Kutsu; illustrated throughout by Pasi Pitkanen.
Authors are Timo Parvela (Finnish) and Bjorn Sortland (Norwegian).
Marketed for readers around 8-12; illustrations run across several pages in places.

books.title: Kepler62: The Virus
books.author: Timo Parvela, Björn Sortland

cz.translator: s přihlédnutím k norskému překladu) Michal Švec a Jitka Jin

flags: Fifth of the six parts published in Czech by Host: Pozvanka, Odpocitavani, Cesta, Prukopnici, Virus, Tajemstvi. Original Finnish title Kepler62 - Kirja 5: Virus.
Illustrated throughout by Pasi Pitkanen; publisher guidance from age nine.
Czech translation by Michal Svec and Jitka Jindrichova, made with reference to the Norwegian text.
The Czech text renders the native people as travni lid; the English edition calls them the Whisperers.

books.title: Komanda Omega
books.author: Jan Kotouč
flags: Volume one of the two-book Centrální impérium: Omega prequel duology (Brokilon 2024, 303 s.); the second volume is listed as Expanzní sektor.
A prequel to the main Centrální impérium series (Hranice impéria, Císař v exilu, Obránci civilizace, Odkaz Protektorů) and readable without it; Hila Ebanová later appears there as empress.
Audiobook read by Kateřina Lojdová; two reviewers disliked the narration specifically, which does not bear on the print edition.
Databáze knih 85 percent from a very small sample (single-digit to low-double-digit ratings), so the aggregate is weak evidence.
No source establishes the chapter-one POV structure.

books.title: Koruna otráveného stromu
books.author: Vlaďka Sacká
flags: The premise ties back to the Philadelphia Experiment of 1943.
Dual narrative between our world and Edegom, with the point of view shifting between characters; one reader describes the transitions as repeated losses of consciousness.

The world contains a prophecy about the Firstborn and the legacy of the Red Empress. No source consulted describes a spell, ritual or incantation enacted on the page - the occult question is argued from the absence of such reports, not from the text.
Reviewers found the pop-culture references excessive, one saying they make it read like fan fiction. Audiobook edition exists.

books.title: Kronovy deti
books.author: Pavel Bares
flags: Czech original; continues Projekt Kronos (Host 2017) and is followed by Kronuv odkaz (2021).
Read in order - the city, cast and epidemic are established in Projekt Kronos.
One Slovak reviewer rates this the strongest volume of the trilogy.

books.title: Kronuv odkaz
books.author: Pavel Bares
flags: Czech original; closes the trilogy after Projekt Kronos (2017) and Kronovy deti (2019).
Read in order - the city, the cast and the war are established in the earlier Host volumes.
A Slovak reviewer judged it a dignified conclusion that does not surpass Kronovy deti and is hurt by a weak start.

books.title: Laila
books.author: Josef Rubáš
flags: Kniha Zlin 2019, Thrill edition, 504 pages; the author's prose debut.
One reader review describes the structure as starting almost at the end and then filling in preceding events.
Czech reader ratings are sharply polarised, from one star to five; no professional literary review was located.

books.title: Láska až za hrob
books.author: Petr Heteša
flags: Epocha 2008, Pevnost edition, 310 pages. Kosmas classifies it as action SF with detective elements.
The author was a figure in 1990s Czech cyberpunk; his novel Sest diamantu (2007) precedes this one in the same edition but the books are separate.
No professional review was located; reception rests on a handful of reader comments and is mixed.

books.title: Departure
books.author: A.G. Riddle
flags: Original title Departure (self-published 2014, HarperCollins 2015). Standalone, not part of the author's Origin Mystery trilogy.
Alternates between two viewpoint characters, Harper and Nick, from early on.

books.title: Space Relic Hunters
books.author: Sylvain Runberg
flags: This is a comics album, not prose: 124 pages, written by Sylvain Runberg with art and colour by Ludovic 'Grun' Dubois.
First album of a series; English edition published by Oni Press as Space Relic Hunters.
Reviewers note repeated jokes about a character's virginity and a hard-drinking lead.

books.title: Metro 2035
books.author: Dmitry Glukhovsky
flags: Continues Dmitry Glukhovsky's Metro 2033 and Metro 2034 - the lead, his wife Anna and the character Sasha are established there.
Reader content warnings for sexual content and sexual violence.
Czech translation by Rudolf Rezabek for Knizni klub.

books.title: Mirzova vize
books.author: Josef Pecinovský
flags: Standalone; Pevnost is the publisher's imprint line, not a story series.
Reviewers independently report the cover art misrepresents the content - there are no dinosaur battles.

books.title: Saturn Run
books.author: John Sandford a Ctein
flags: Standalone; credited to John Sandford and Ctein.
Reviewers report a pacing sag during the months of transit and a hurried ending.
Background elements (the Tri-Border Fight, the Houston Flash, universal implants) are asserted and never explained.
Czech translation Marek Ctrnact, Dobrovsky 2018.

books.title: Misteri
books.author: Jana Rečková
flags: Epocha 2018, edice Pevnost; catalogue headings thrillery (romany) and vedecko-fantasticke romany.
Author died in March 2018; no reviews or reader ratings of this title were located.
Czech original, no translation involved.

books.title: Les hommes proteges
books.author: Robert Merle
flags: Original Les hommes proteges (1974); English translation The Virility Factor.
The catalogue also holds an earlier print translation (Svoboda 1985, same translator Zdenek Frybort) and an audio edition (Macanova knihovna 2011).
Satirises feminist and sexist positions alike; the author stated he did not intend an anti-feminist book. Heavily of its 1970s moment.
A German-set film adaptation, The Protected Men, was in international sales as of 2024.

books.title: Ascension
books.author: Nicholas Binge
flags: Standalone, epistolary, framed as recovered letters with an afterword by a family member.
Editions differ (Riverhead in the US, HarperVoyager in the UK); Czech translation Julie Tesla, Dobrovsky 2023.
The catalogue heading calls it a thriller; the content is speculative with horror elements.

books.title: Nad ceskymi zememi slunce nezapada
books.author: Jan Kotouč
flags: Volume one of a six-book series (Brokilon 2016, 317 s., cover by Tomáš Flak); Ofenziva českých zemí 2017, V tajné službě Koruny české 2019, Spojenci českých zemí 2020, Bitva o české země 2022 follow.
A second print edition appeared in 2022 (Brokilon, ISBN 978-80-7456-523-6); an audiobook and an ebook also exist.
Databáze knih shows 82 percent from around 363 ratings, against a strongly negative review on sarden.cz - a split typical of genre-audience satisfaction rather than critical approval.
Occult status not examined - the ladder exits before that gate on a book that lands below the propose line either way.

books.title: A Beautifully Foolish Endeavor
books.author: Hank Green
flags: Continues An Absolutely Remarkable Thing (Czech: Naprosto pozoruhodna vec) and assumes its ending; the lead of that book is absent for much of this one.
Narrated in first person by several alternating characters rather than by the previous single narrator.

prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: Navigators of Dune
books.author: Brian Herbert, Kevin J. Anderson
flags: Written by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson, not Frank Herbert; original Navigators of Dune (2016).
Concludes the Schools of Dune trilogy after Sisterhood of Dune and Mentats of Dune, and depends on them; those two are not in the catalogue record given here.

prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: More Than This
books.author: Patrick Ness
flags: The simulation reveal arrives roughly 150 pages in, when two other survivors appear.
Recurring content: suicide and suicidal ideation, domestic abuse, child abuse, homophobia; the lead's outing and the end of his relationship with a boyfriend is the cause of his death.
Reviewers describe the ending as deliberately open and are split on whether that works.

books.title: Star Trek: Voyager: Unworthy
books.author: Kirsten Beyer
flags: Depends on a run of earlier novels: Before Dishonor, Greater Than the Sum, the three-volume Destiny series and Full Circle; the Caeliar are introduced in Destiny.
Reviewers describe Full Circle and Unworthy as functioning as a pair.

books.title: Neni krve bez ohne
books.author: Jiří W. Procházka
flags: Volume two of the multi-author Agent John Francis Kovář series; first published by Triton in 2005 and reissued in 2017. The series was created by Jiří Walker Procházka and Miroslav Žamboch on the Perry Rhodan / Mark Stone dime-novel model, with contributions from Ondřej Neff, Vladimír Šlechta, Karolina Francová and others.
Written and published around the bicentenary of Austerlitz.
Volume one, Pašerák (Triton 2005), was co-written by Procházka and Žamboch and introduces Agency EF.
Occult status not examined - the ladder exits before that gate.

books.title: Neočekávaný robotí exodus
books.author: Taťána Rubášová, Jindřich Janíček
flags: Second part of the Czech comics trilogy about William and Meriwether: Podivuhodna roboti expedice (2016), Neocekavany roboti exodus (2019), Strastiplna roboti existence (2023).
Ninety-six page softcover comics album; catalogue heading komiksy / publikace pro mladez.
Czech original, no translation involved.

books.title: Nyxia Unleashed
books.author: Scott Reintgen
flags: Second of Scott Reintgen's Nyxia Triad; continues Nyxia and is followed by Nyxia povstava.
Read in order - the lead, the contract and the crew are established in Nyxia.

books.title: Nyxia Uprising
books.author: Scott Reintgen
flags: Closes Scott Reintgen's Nyxia Triad after Nyxia and Nyxia nespoutana.
Read in order - the crew, the corporation and the Imago are established in the earlier volumes.

books.title: Nyxia
books.author: Scott Reintgen
flags: First of Scott Reintgen's Nyxia Triad; continues in Czech as Nyxia nespoutana and Nyxia povstava.
Reader content warnings for the series include violence, torture, PTSD and genocide; no reviewer flagged sexual content.

books.title: Obranci civilizace
books.author: Jan Kotouč
flags: Volume three of the Centrální impérium series (Fantom Print 2020); preceded by Hranice impéria and Císař v exilu, followed by Odkaz Protektorů (2020).
Depends on the preceding volumes - the emperor, the New Protectorate and the political situation are established there.
The screen-infidelity lexicon flagged 'svadi' in the annotation; in context this is 'svádí válku' (wages war), not an affair.
No source establishes the chapter-one POV structure.

books.title: Distortion
books.author: Victor Dixen
flags: Czech edition of Distortion, the second of Victor Dixen's Phobos series; it continues Vyslani (Ascension) and is followed in Czech by Stretnuti and Ohrozeni.
Read in order - the lead and the Genesis premise are introduced in Vyslani.

books.title: Odkaz Protektoru
books.author: Jan Kotouč
flags: Volume four of the Centrální impérium series (Fantom Print 2020); preceded by Hranice impéria, Císař v exilu and Obránci civilizace.
Depends heavily on the preceding volumes - the New Protectorate war, Hila Ebanová and the family politics are all established there.
Hila Ebanová, the emperor's wife here, is the lead of the separate prequel duology Centrální impérium: Omega (Brokilon 2024).
No source establishes the chapter-one POV structure.

books.title: Ophelia Scale: Die Welt wird brennen
books.author: Lena Kiefer
flags: Book one of a trilogy: Die Welt wird brennen, Der Himmel wird beben, Die Sterne werden fallen, plus an e-book short story Wie alles begann. It ends on a cliffhanger.
Marketed as young adult; German reviewers compare it to The Hunger Games.
Reviewed almost exclusively by bloggers and reader-review sites, not professional critics.

books.title: Ofenziva ceskych zemi
books.author: Jan Kotouč
flags: Volume two of a six-book series (Brokilon 2017), following Nad českými zeměmi slunce nezapadá (2016); V tajné službě Koruny české 2019, Spojenci českých zemí 2020 and Bitva o české země 2022 come after.
Marketed as the sequel to the earlier bestseller and depends on it for the setting, though the annotation re-states the premise.
Occult status not examined - the ladder exits before that gate.

books.title: Phobos 4
books.author: Victor Dixen
flags: Czech edition of the fourth Phobos book by Victor Dixen; it follows Vyslani (Ascension), Odchyleni (Distortion) and Stretnuti (Collision).
The Czech volumes Ohrozeni and Stretnuti both appeared in 2025; Stretnuti is the earlier story.

books.title: Opraváři času
books.author: Naďa Reviláková
flags: First of a series; Opravari casu: Tajna organizace and Opravari casu: Hlubiny temne minulosti follow.
Dobrovsky (Drobek imprint). The catalogue holds both a 2024 and a 2025 printing; sources give 2024 as the first edition.
Publisher recommends age 8 and up; one reviewer suggests 10 and up. Rated around 90 percent on Databaze knih.

books.title: Pachatelé zvláštních činů
books.author: Jana Rečková
flags: Epocha 2009, edice Pevnost sv. 46, 248 pages; five linked stories - Narodila ses jako vrah, Nesmrtelnost, nic vic, Vrazda na piskovisti, Dovolena mise, Jako spiknuti - and the set is sometimes described as a novel.
The text dates from the first half of the 1990s; a few samizdat copies appeared in 1995.
Author died in 2018; no published reviews of this title were located.

books.title: Paul of Dune
books.author: Brian Herbert, Kevin J. Anderson
flags: Written by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson, not Frank Herbert; original Paul of Dune (2008).
Set between Frank Herbert's Dune and Dune Messiah and depends on both; first of the Heroes of Dune pair, before The Winds of Dune.

books.title: Písečníci a bludný asteroid
books.author: Václav Dvořák
flags: Book one of the Pisecnici series; self-published 2018, 366 pages, cover and illustrations by Jakub Cenkl.
Reviewers recommend age 10+, and note some of the name humour only works for adults.
Reader comments on Dobrovsky and Goodreads repeatedly compare it to Harry Potter, meaning the school-and-adventure shape rather than any magic.
Testimonials on the author's own site are curated marketing material, not independent reviews.

books.title: Podhoubi smrti
books.author: Jiří W. Procházka

cz.publisher: Ve spolupráci s EF vydalo nakl. Triton

flags: Volume 11 of the multi-author Agent John Francis Kovář series (Triton, in cooperation with EF, 2007), created by Jiří Walker Procházka and Miroslav Žamboch on the Perry Rhodan / Mark Stone dime-novel model.
The Agency EF setting and the lead are established in earlier volumes of the shared series, starting with Pašerák (2005).
Occult status not examined - the ladder exits before that gate.

books.title: Greybeard
books.author: Brian Wilson Aldiss
flags: Original title Greybeard (1964).
Structure alternates: odd chapters the journey, even chapters flashbacks to the years just after the sterilisation.
Rumours of elves and gnomes in the woods are folklore reported by characters, not a magic system; no occult practice appears.
Routinely shelved alongside P. D. James's The Children of Men, which shares the premise.

books.title: Poločas rozpadu
books.author: František Kotleta
flags: Second of four: after Spad, before Razova vlna and Retezova reakce; described by the publisher as a loose continuation of Spad.
Frantisek Kotleta is the pen name of Leos Kysa.
A 688-page omnibus of all four was published by Epocha in 2022.

books.title: Posledni velkomesto
books.author: Vladimir Slechta
flags: Part of the five-book Posledni velkomesto cycle (Tajna historie Bornnu 2018, Kletba, Padajici Archandel, Bila jako sul 2023), which itself continues Slechta's older Oggerd books.
The catalogue record covers several Brokilon printings (2019, 2020, 2022, 2023), so the exact volume behind this record is ambiguous.
Narrated in the first person by Gowery as a retrospective memoir addressed to a later audience.
The author's Oggerd world mixes post-apocalyptic SF with fantasy elements; his other cycles (Likarijske, Krvave pohranici) contain orcs and elves.

books.title: The Postman
books.author: David Brin
flags: Assembled from earlier novellas, which is why reviewers describe it as reading in distinct movements of declining quality.
A 1997 film adaptation exists and differs substantially, including in the scene noted below.

The 'body father' episode involves a married woman asking the protagonist to conceive a child; the sources show her husband as a knowing party and a village elder as broker, so it is a sanctioned arrangement and not a betrayal - the infidelity axis was examined and does not apply.
Reviewers widely criticise the novel's handling of its women characters and its 'straw feminist' faction.

books.title: Foundation's Friends: Stories in Honor of Isaac Asimov
books.author: Martin H. Greenberg (editor)
flags: Original anthology Foundation's Friends: Stories in Honor of Isaac Asimov (1989), edited by Martin H. Greenberg.
Contributors include Orson Scott Card ('The Originist', a Foundation novella), Connie Willis, Harry Turtledove, Frederik Pohl, Poul Anderson, Robert Silverberg and Mike Resnick.
Two pieces are mystery-shaped: Edward Wellen's Wendell Urth story and Edward D. Hoch's Black Widowers story.
Later editions add an 'Appreciations' section of non-fiction tributes.

books.title: Projekt Kronos
books.author: Pavel Bares
flags: Czech original; the trilogy continues with Kronovy deti (2019) and Kronuv odkaz (2021).
The Host edition carries black-and-white chapter illustrations.
Bares also wrote the standalone Meta (2020).

books.title: Wanderers
books.author: Chuck Wendig
flags: Wanderers, Del Rey 2019, roughly 800 pages; a sequel, Wayward, follows and this book stands alone.
Czech edition Euromedia Group's Laser imprint 2021, translated by Daniela Orlando.
Chapter one is a single concrete situation, but four viewpoint characters are running by mid-book: Shana, Benji, an aging rock star and a radio pastor.
Sexual content was not established from the sources used; on-page gore and militia violence are reported.

books.title: Good Morning, Midnight
books.author: Lily Brooks-Daltonova
flags: Original title Good Morning, Midnight (2016), the author's debut novel; about 290 pages.
Chapters alternate between the two viewpoint characters throughout.
Adapted as the Netflix film The Midnight Sky (2020).

books.title: Rázová vlna
books.author: František Kotleta
flags: Third of four: after Spad and Polocas rozpadu, before Retezova reakce.
Frantisek Kotleta is the pen name of Leos Kysa.
A 688-page omnibus of all four was published by Epocha in 2022.

books.title: Reborn
books.author: Alex Scarrow
flags: Second part of the trilogy; follows Remade (UK paperback Plague Land) and precedes Plague World. It opens eighteen months to two years after the first book and continues its leads.
Catalogued as publikace pro mladez.
Czech edition Dobrovsky 2020, translated by Aneta Zemankova.

books.title: Remade
books.author: Alex Scarrow
flags: Published in UK/US paperback as Plague Land; first part of the trilogy Remade / Reborn (Plague Nation) / Plague World.
Catalogued as publikace pro mladez; publisher guidance around ages 13-14.
Czech edition Dobrovsky 2019, translated by Aneta Zemankova.

books.title: Řetězová reakce
books.author: František Kotleta
flags: Fourth and last of the sequence, after Spad, Polocas rozpadu and Razova vlna.
Frantisek Kotleta is the pen name of Leos Kysa.
A 688-page omnibus of all four was published by Epocha in 2022.

books.title: SPAD
books.author: František Kotleta
flags: First of four: Spad, Polocas rozpadu, Razova vlna, Retezova reakce; a 688-page omnibus was published by Epocha in 2022.
Frantisek Kotleta is the pen name of Leos Kysa.
Translated into English as This World of Ours: Fallout.
Databaze knih content tags for the series include violence, brutality and slavery.

books.title: Spojenci ceskych zemi
books.author: Jan Kotouč
flags: Volume four of a six-book series (Brokilon 2020); preceded by Nad českými zeměmi slunce nezapadá (2016), Ofenziva českých zemí (2017) and V tajné službě Koruny české (2019), followed by Bitva o české země (2022).
Depends on the preceding volumes for the war situation, though the annotation re-states the flooded-world premise.
Occult status not examined - the ladder exits before that gate.

books.title: Battlecry (Sten omnibus 1)
books.author: Chris Bunch, Allan Cole
flags: Czech omnibus, Triton 2023; original title Battlecry, collecting the opening books of the eight-novel Sten Adventures (Sten 1982, The Wolf Worlds 1984).
The series ran 1982-1993 with later additions by Cole; the Emperor's benevolence is reexamined in later books.
Czech translation Zdenek Uhercik.

books.title: Stín mrtvého
books.author: Josef Pecinovský
flags: A volume of two separate novellas, Stin kobry and Zabit mrtveho, with no shared characters or setting.
Readers rate Stin kobry clearly above Zabit mrtveho.
The second novella's reincarnation premise was not checked against the occult filter at this exit.

books.title: Stranger Things: Suspicious Minds
books.author: Gwenda Bond
flags: The first of the official Stranger Things tie-in novels; a prequel to the series, set before it.
One unverified report claims the 2019 text was revised after the show's fourth season.

books.title: Stranger Things: Rebel Robin
books.author: A. R. Capetta
