flags: Original title Stranger Things: Rebel Robin (2021), a prequel to season 3 covering the period of season 1.
Fourth of the Stranger Things tie-in novels; a companion scripted podcast, Rebel Robin: Surviving Hawkins, was released alongside it.
Catalogue keyword is 'sci-fi'; catalogue headings also list it as a girls' novel for young adults.
Content notes from reviewers: bullying, homophobia and internalised homophobia, discussion of racism.
A second Stranger Things tie-in is held in Czech translation: Suyi Davies, Lucas on the Line (Argo 2023).

books.title: Stranger Things: Lucas on the Line
books.author: Suyi Davies
flags: Original title Stranger Things: Lucas on the Line (2022), fifth of the Stranger Things tie-in novels; set after season 3 and overlapping part of season 4.
Parts 1-4 are a standalone school-year narrative; Part 5 joins the televised storyline.
Author also publishes adult SF and fantasy as Suyi Davies Okungbowa.
A second Stranger Things tie-in is held in Czech translation: A. R. Capetta, Rebel Robin (Argo 2022).

books.title: Stranger Things: Runaway Max
books.author: Brenna Yovanoffová
flags: Third book in the Stranger Things tie-in novel line, after Suspicious Minds and Darkness on the Edge of Town; it retells season two from Max's viewpoint and does not require the other two novels.
Shelved middle grade by the publisher but reviewers report a YA feel and on-page physical abuse of Billy by his father, Neil Hargrove.
Czech edition Argo 2021, translated by Michala Markova.

books.title: Collision
books.author: Victor Dixen
flags: Czech edition of Collision, the third of Victor Dixen's Phobos series; it follows Vyslani (Ascension) and Odchyleni (Distortion).
The Czech volume Ohrozeni, published the same year, corresponds to the later Phobos 4 - read Stretnuti first.

books.title: Studené světlo hvězd
books.author: Pavel Fritz
flags: Epocha 2021, 520 pages, the opening title of the Jine svety edition; reprinted 2025.
One of the ten texts overlaps the author's earlier collection Archa zrud, and readers report having met some pieces before.
Rated around 90 percent on Databaze knih across 200-plus ratings; a Czech audiobook read by Filip Jancik exists.
The author's earlier books are Letka 307, Pristav u reky Styx and Archa zrud.

books.title: Svět v bouři
books.author: Kristýna Sněgoňová
flags: Third part of the Mesta trilogy: Mesto v oblacich (2020), Zeme v troskach (2021), Svet v bouri (2022).
Reviewers state it opens by returning to characters from the previous book and advise against reading it on its own, in contrast to Zeme v troskach.
Czech original; audiobook exists from Audioteka/Epocha, read by Martin Preiss, about 10h47.

books.title: Světelné (k)roky
books.author: Petr Rušeb
flags: The book's full title is Svetelne (k)roky: Galakticka vyprava posledniho cloveka ve vesmiru; the catalogue records it as Svetelne kroky.
The author won the first Spisovatelsky startovac competition; Fobos/Nase nakladatelstvi 2025. Databaze knih shows 55% from two ratings, so there is effectively no aggregate reception.
Divided into four parts and supplied with an intergalactic glossary.
Audiobook edition exists.

books.title: Světlo pulsaru
books.author: Aleš Pitzmos
flags: First book of the Vesmirna asociace series; Zare supernovy, Jas kvasaru and Svit magnetaru follow.
Brokilon 2015, 336 pages, in the Evropska space opera line.
Reviewed by Jan Nohovec on fantasya.cz and by Rastislav Weber on fandom.sk; neither full text was read.

books.title: Star Trek: Titan - Synthesis
books.author: James Swallow
flags: Sixth novel in the Star Trek: Titan line and the first in it by James Swallow; set after the Star Trek: Destiny trilogy, whose aftermath the crew is still dealing with.
Czech edition Euromedia 2019, translated by Jakub Marek.

prereq.ref: (Star Trek: Titan #1-3, not on the shelf)
prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: The Dark Forest
books.author: Liou Cch'-sin
books.series: Vzpominka na Zemi (Remembrance of Earth's Past)
flags: Published in Czech as Liou Cch'-sin; English editions use Liu Cixin. Czech translation by Ales Drobek for Host.
Continues Problem tri teles - read that first; the trilogy closes with Death's End, not covered here.
The English edition is by a different translator than the first book, and reviewers report a drop in prose quality there; the Czech run keeps one translator throughout.
Volume 1, Problem tri teles, was read to p. 200 and dropped (2026-10-29, scored 62): this volume cannot be read without it.

books.title: Where Do We Go From Here?
books.author: sestavil Isaac Asimov
flags: Original anthology Where Do We Go From Here? (1971).
The 2011 Triton printing is the first complete Czech edition; the 1979 Czech edition omitted five stories.
Each story carries an editorial science commentary, so part of the volume is non-fiction apparatus.
Publisher's contents list carries two propagated errors: 'Don A. Stuart' is John W. Campbell's pen name and 'Walter S. Trevis' is Walter Tevis.

books.title: Star Trek: Typhon Pact: Zero Sum Game
books.author: David Mack
flags: Opens a four-book Typhon Pact sequence and follows on from the Destiny trilogy's post-war politics; one reviewer says it stands alone if you know who Bashir is.
The Bashir-Douglas romance involves no marriage or engagement, so the infidelity axis was not in play.

books.title: Útěk z Arestonu
books.author: Josef Pecinovský
flags: Second of the Areston trilogy, after Areston and before Vladce Arestonu; the lead and the prison are introduced in the first book and assumed here.
A companion volume, Stavitele Arestonu, is reported by readers to restate information already given.

books.title: The Prey
books.author: Tom Isbell
flags: Book one of a trilogy (The Prey / The Capture / The Release); only this volume was checked for a Czech route.
Marketed by the publisher as 'The Maze Runner meets The Hunger Games'.

books.title: Utopia
books.author: Thomas More
flags: Two books: the first a dialogue between More, Peter Giles and Raphael Hythloday, the second Hythloday's uninterrupted description of the island. Erasmus records that the second was written first.
The narrator's name means roughly 'expert in nonsense', and scholars dispute how far More endorses the institutions described.
Utopian institutions described include enslavement as the usual sentence for serious crime, and priests and magistrates urging the incurably ill to end their own lives.
This Karolinum 2024 edition reissues Bohumil Ryba's translation with notes, in a history-of-political-philosophy series.

books.title: Perdus dans le Glitchox-verse
books.author: Léonard Bertos
flags: An unofficial fan novel, not a licensed product of the game.

Identification of the French original rests on matching the characters Nora, Sami and Capucine and the Glitchox roulette premise to the 404 editions junior novel by Leonard Bertos (2023, ~293 pp, marketed for ages 8-13); the exact French title on the catalogue record could not be traced, so the author attribution carries that uncertainty.
The Czech catalogue record credits only the translator, not an author.

books.title: V tajne sluzbe Koruny ceske
books.author: Jan Kotouč
flags: Volume three of a six-book series (Brokilon 2019); preceded by Nad českými zeměmi slunce nezapadá (2016) and Ofenziva českých zemí (2017), followed by Spojenci českých zemí (2020) and Bitva o české země (2022).
Espionage and sabotage plot - investigation-shaped material, but not a whodunnit; noted rather than treated as the detective filter.
Occult status not examined - the ladder exits before that gate.

books.title: Ve jmenu zitrka
books.author: Thomas Blanc
flags: Czech original, 2019, the author's debut; small publisher (Credit-plus / Kniha.je).
A sequel titled 'Usvit temne noci' was announced in the back of the book but appears never to have been published.
The author has since moved to gothic horror set at the end of Austria-Hungary.

books.title: Vesmirna zasilkovna
books.author: Klara Smolikova
flags: Pikola imprint (Euromedia), 2023; 112 pages, illustrated by Martin Hanschild.
Catalogue heading is 'publikace pro deti'; reviewers recommend it for ages roughly 7-10 and for first independent reading.
Contains interspersed factual notes and short quizzes for children.

books.title: The Oracle Year
books.author: Charles Soule
flags: The Oracle Year, Harper Perennial 2018, 416 pages; a standalone.
A manhunt for the Oracle's identity runs through the book, but the payoff is consequence and thriller rather than whodunnit.

The predictions arrive unexplained in a dream and are not obtained by any rite; whether any devotional scene is enacted on the page was not established from a source, so occult clearance here is inferred rather than sourced.
Czech edition Euromedia 2018, translated by Milan Lzicka.

books.title: The Winds of Dune
books.author: Brian Herbert, Kevin J. Anderson
flags: Written by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson, not Frank Herbert; original The Winds of Dune (2009).
Begins where Frank Herbert's Dune Messiah ends and depends on it; second of the Heroes of Dune pair, after Paul of Dune.

books.title: Vládce Arestonu
books.author: Josef Pecinovský
flags: Third and closing volume of the Areston trilogy, after Areston and Utek z Arestonu; the lead, the object and the code plot are all established there and assumed here.
Readers report a number of questions remain unexplained even after the companion volume Stavitele Arestonu.

books.title: The Wolves of Winter
books.author: Tyrell Johnson
flags: The Wolves of Winter, Scribner 2018; a debut novel and a standalone.
The late-arriving science-fiction turn is the most-criticised element in reviews; reader consensus is otherwise favourable on atmosphere and setting.
Czech edition Dobrovsky 2018 in the Fobos line, translated by Martina Simova.

books.title: Vyměřený čas
books.author: Karel Cubeca
flags: Karel Cubeca is a pseudonym of Karel Kostka (b. 1960, Vsetin).
Alpress, edition Klokan, 384 pages, 2019; retailers file it under adventure/thriller rather than science fiction.
One reader review states the action takes place on Mars rather than Earth.
No professional Czech genre-press review found; ratings come from bookseller and reader-database sites (81% from 32 reader ratings on Databaze knih).

books.title: Ascension
books.author: Victor Dixen
flags: Czech edition of Ascension, the first of Victor Dixen's French Phobos series (Robert Laffont); the Czech run continues as Odchyleni, Stretnuti and Ohrozeni.
Reviewers report it ends on a cliffhanger and is published for ages 13+.

books.title: Hammered
books.author: Elizabeth Bear
flags: First part of the Jenny Casey trilogy (Hammered / Scardown / Worldwired); reviewers report it does not stand alone and that Scardown resumes immediately after it.
Won the Locus Award for Best First Novel, 2006.
Czech edition Laser 2009, translated by Tadeas Pelech.

books.title: Earth Abides
books.author: George R. Stewart
flags: The catalogue record misspells the author as 'George R. Srewart'.
First winner of the International Fantasy Award (1951).

Sunday Bible readings and a burial service are shown, and the tribe comes to treat the protagonist's hammer as semi-sacred; the reverence is narrated as cultural drift, with no occult rite performed on the page.

books.title: Země v troskách
books.author: Kristýna Sněgoňová
flags: Second part of the Mesta trilogy: Mesto v oblacich (2020), Zeme v troskach (2021), Svet v bouri (2022); reviewers say this one can be read on its own, unlike the third.
Czech original; audiobook from Audioteka/Epocha read by Martin Preiss.

books.title: Tierra
books.author: Eloy Moreno
flags: Around 550 pages; Ediciones B, Spain, 2020.
One press summary states the eight contestants are sent to Mars, which the publisher's own synopsis avoids saying - treat that as a possible spoiler or misreading.

books.title: Scardown
books.author: Elizabeth Bear
flags: Second part of the Jenny Casey trilogy (Hammered / Scardown / Worldwired); it resumes directly from Hammered and reviewers compare the join to The Two Towers following The Fellowship.
Czech edition Laser 2011, translated by Tadeas Pelech.

books.title: Star Trek: Crucible: Kirk - The Star to Every Wandering
books.author: David R. George III
flags: Third of three Crucible novels (McCoy, Spock, Kirk), each built around the episode 'The City on the Edge of Forever'; reviewers rank McCoy highest.
Assumes the events of the film Star Trek: Generations.

prereq.ref: (Star Trek: Crucible #1-2, not on the shelf)
prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: Mass Effect: Deception
books.author: William C. Dietz
flags: Fourth Mass Effect novel, after Revelation, Ascension and Retribution by Drew Karpyshyn; the plot continues Gillian Grayson's story from Retribution and assumes it rather than re-establishing it.
Widely treated as outside Mass Effect continuity. BioWare and Del Rey issued a public apology for the errors and the promised corrected edition never appeared.
Czech edition Fantom Print 2012, translated by Jakub Marik.

prereq.ref: (Mass Effect: Revelation, Ascension and Retribution, not on the shelf)
prereq.note: The plot continues the earlier Mass Effect novels.

books.title: Strastiplná robotí existence
books.author: Taťána Rubášová, Jindřich Janíček
flags: Third and final part of the Czech comics trilogy about William and Meriwether: Podivuhodna roboti expedice (2016), Neocekavany roboti exodus (2019), Strastiplna roboti existence (2023).
Ninety-six page softcover comics album; the catalogue heading is publikace pro deti / sci-fi komiksy, and the theme is recorded as dystopie.
Czech original, no translation involved.

books.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey / The Fountains of Paradise
books.author: Arthur C. Clarke
flags: One volume holding two separate novels: 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968) and The Fountains of Paradise (1979).
2001 has three sequels (2010, 2061, 3001); The Fountains of Paradise is standalone and won both the Hugo and the Nebula.
The Fountains of Paradise closes with an ancient prophecy fulfilled by a swarm of butterflies, played as irony rather than reverence.
The novel's Discovery flies to Saturn, not to Jupiter as in the film.
Czech: Odeon 1988; the catalogue record lists no translator.

books.title: Highfire
books.author: Eoin Colfer
flags: Colfer's first novel written for adults, distinct from his Artemis Fowl books.
Heavy profanity and gore per reviews.

books.title: The Running Man
books.author: Richard Bachman (Stephen King)
flags: Published 1982 as by Richard Bachman, King's pseudonym; a standalone novel, not part of a series.
101 short chapters in a countdown structure, from 'Minus 100' to 'Minus 000'.
The 1987 and 2025 films both change the ending substantially; the novel ends with the protagonist's death.
Graphic injury detail in the climax.

books.title: The Road to the Rim
books.author: A. Bertram Chandler
flags: The Road to the Rim (1967), 117 pp, first of the John Grimes sequence.
To Prime the Pump follows it and stages a Black Arts goat-sacrifice scene.
Reprinted in the Baen omnibus To the Galactic Rim (2011).
Czech: Wales 2004; the catalogue record gives the translator only as 'P'.

books.title: Doctor Who: 11 Doctors, 11 Stories
books.author: Eoin Colfer, Michael Scott, Marcus Sedgwick, Philip Reeve, Patrick Ness, Richelle Mead, Malorie Blackman, Alex Scarrow, Charlie Higson, Derek Landy, Neil Gaiman
flags: Published in English as 11 Doctors, 11 Stories by Puffin, November 2013, for the fiftieth anniversary of the series; a licensed tie-in to the television programme.
Contributors' stories include Charlie Higson's 'The Beast of Babylon' and Neil Gaiman's contribution.
Czech edition Jota 2015, translated by Vera Kovarova.

books.title: The Ascension Factor
books.author: Frank Herbert & Bill Ransom
flags: Fourth and final book of the Pandora sequence, after Destination: Void, The Jesus Incident and The Lazarus Effect; set about twenty-five years after The Lazarus Effect and continuing its characters and situation.
Published 1988, after Frank Herbert's death.
None of the preceding volumes is excluded on a taste filter, so nothing is inherited; this is a dependency note only.

prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: Hrdinové českých zemí
books.author: Jan Kotouč (ed.)
flags: Part of Jan Kotouč's České země sequence, following the novels Nad českými zeměmi slunce nezapadá (2016) and Ofenziva českých zemí (2017); catalogued as the sixth title in that line.
Contributors include Tomáš Bandžuch, Marek Brenišin, Vendula Brunhoferová, Karel Doležal, Lucie Lukačovičová, Julie Nováková, Joelle Presby, Vlado Ríša and Vladimír Šlechta, plus the editor.
Afterword by Boris Hokr. 426 pages, Brokilon Alternativa imprint.
Kotouč's story 'Po velké bouři' also appeared in the anthology Ve stínu apokalypsy.

books.title: Kotlovan (The Foundation Pit)
books.author: Andrej Platonov
flags: Academic edition: reconstructs the original text and is accompanied by Natalja Dužinová's companion, Průvodce Jámou.
Written 1930, unpublishable in the Soviet Union until 1987.
A short novel, and a modernist one - the prose is deliberately deformed, which the Czech edition annotates extensively.
Multiple viewpoint characters (Voschev, Prushevsky, Chiklin and others) rather than a single protagonist.

books.title: The Currents of Space
books.author: Isaac Asimov
flags: Second of Asimov's three Galactic Empire novels, self-contained, set some fifteen thousand years before Foundation.

Mystery-shaped: the plot is the recovery of an erased memory and it closes with the person behind the psycho-probe identified. Judged an investigation-shaped structure inside an SF political novel rather than a detective novel, so flagged rather than rejected.
Czech: Triton/Argo 2009, prel. Jindrich Smekal.

books.title: The Boat of a Million Years
books.author: Poul Anderson
flags: Episodic structure: successive chapters follow different immortals in different eras, and the surviving eight only converge near the end.
Hugo and Nebula finalist, 1990; a New York Times Notable Book.
The catalogue record for the 2001 Classic edition lists no translator.
The earliest section is set in prehistory; the first extended sequence pairs the Phoenician Hanno with the historical Greek explorer Pytheas of Massalia.

books.title: The Possibility of an Island
books.author: Michel Houellebecq
flags: La possibilite d'une ile (2005); the sect is modelled on the real Raelian movement.
The narrative alternates the original narrator's memoir with commentary by later clones, so two frames are live throughout.
Czech: Odeon 2021, prel. Jovanka Sotolova.

books.title: Off on a Comet (Hector Servadac)
books.author: Jules Verne
flags: Also known as Hector Servadac (1877).
The widely circulated English text is an altered and later shortened translation; the Czech route is translated from the French by Bedrich Fricke.
The character Isac Hakhabut is a Jewish caricature that reviewers regularly single out.
Czech: Dobrovsky 2016.

books.title: Foundation and Empire
books.author: Isaac Asimov
flags: Follows Foundation and assumes the Seldon Plan and the Foundation's early history rather than re-establishing them.
Second of the original Foundation trilogy; Second Foundation continues the Mule story.
Built from two novellas, The General and The Mule; the second won a retrospective Hugo in 1996.
Czech: Argo 2009, prel. Viktor Janis.

books.title: Invisibly Yours
books.author: C. D. Payne
flags: Original title Invisibly Yours (2010); Czech translation by Richard Janda, 250 pages.
Appears to be self- or small-press published in English - no trade or literary press reviews exist, only reader reviews.
By the author of Youth in Revolt; Jota has published several of his other novels in Czech.

books.title: Tales Before Tolkien: The Roots of Modern Fantasy
books.author: Douglas A. Anderson (ed.)
flags: English original Tales Before Tolkien: The Roots of Modern Fantasy, Ballantine 2003, edited by Douglas A. Anderson.
The catalogue record describes the contents as excerpts from works; the English anthology prints complete short pieces, so the Czech volume may be an abridged selection.
Anderson is a Tolkien scholar, editor of the annotated Hobbit; a companion volume, Tales Before Narnia, exists.
The catalogue gives no translator.

books.title: The Last Ringbearer (Poslednij kolcenosec)
books.author: Kiril Yeskov
flags: A revisionist retelling of The Lord of the Rings; the same characters and events appear, and reviewers say prior knowledge of Tolkien is essential rather than optional.
Originally published in Russian (1999); an unauthorised English fan translation circulated widely, and the Czech Fantom Print 2003 edition is a licensed print translation.
Reconnaissance and forgery plot with several viewpoint strands; not an investigation, so the detective bar does not apply.
The catalogue gives no translator for the Czech edition.

books.title: Tales of the Peculiar
books.author: Ransom Riggs
flags: Companion volume to Riggs's Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children sequence; reviewers say it reads standalone, and compare its function to The Tales of Beedle the Bard.
About 160 pages, illustrated by Andrew Davidson.

prereq.ref: (Sirotčinec slečny Peregrinové #2-6, not on the shelf)
prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: Psí zima
books.author: Petra Neomillnerová
flags: A sequel: the story preceding it is Zaklínačka Lota (Motto), a story collection covering Lota's life up to this novel.
Author and reviewers place the series in the 'dirty fantasy' register - open depiction of violence and sex, first person, present tense.
Czech original; no translation involved.

books.title: Shadow Show: All-New Stories in Celebration of Ray Bradbury
books.author: Sam Weller, Mort Castle (eds.)
flags: Bradbury died a month before publication, which turned an intended celebration into a memorial volume.
Contributors include Margaret Atwood, Neil Gaiman, Harlan Ellison, Kelly Link, Joe Hill, Ramsey Campbell, Dave Eggers, Audrey Niffenegger and Robert McCammon.
A five-issue IDW comics adaptation of the anthology appeared in 2014; the Czech route here is the prose edition, not that adaptation.

books.title: The Fantasy Hall of Fame
books.author: Robert Silverberg (ed.)
flags: The catalogue also holds another print edition: Baronet 2004.
The Czech publication splits the anthology into volumes; this is the first.

Two English anthologies carry this title - a 1983 volume edited by Silverberg with Martin H. Greenberg, and a 1998 volume edited by Silverberg alone; the writers'-ballot selection described in the record matches the latter.
The catalogue gives no translator.

books.title: Stravaganza: City of Masks
books.author: Mary Hoffmanova
flags: First book of Hoffman's Stravaganza sequence; later volumes continue with other travellers.
The catalogue gives no translator for the Czech edition.
The lead's friendship with Arianna becomes a betrothal in a later volume, not in this one.

books.title: The Holy War Made by Shaddai upon Diabolus
books.author: John Bunyan
books.czTitle: Svata valka, kterou vedl Saddaj s Diabolem o hlavni mesto sveta, aneb, Ztrata a znovuziskani mesta Duse
flags: Prose allegory of 1682, not a novel in form; 'novel' is the nearest available value.
Companion piece to Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress, which is a separate work and not required reading for this one.
The opening structure was not established - the C exit stopped research before that check.

books.title: The World at the End of Time
books.author: Frederik Pohl
flags: Published 1990; a standalone novel, not part of Pohl's Heechee sequence.

books.title: Svet uzasny jako kapka jedu
books.author: Zdenek Volny
flags: Czech original; no translation involved.
Draws on the earlier collections Nedele na prodej and Zlata past plna casu.
Most of the material dates from the 1980s.

books.title: Terra nullius
books.author: Julie Nováková (ed.)
flags: Editorial debut of Julie Nováková, who also contributed a story ('Zaříkávač lodí'); published in the Brokilon Alternativa imprint.
Contributors include Martin Gilar, Tomáš Petrásek, Tomáš Dostál, Karolína Francová, Alexandr Kazda, Petra Pecharová, Lucie Lukačovičová and Hanuš Seiner.
Czech originals; no translation involved.

books.title: Tolkien a jeho tajemný svět
books.author: Édouard Kloczko
flags: Thirty-two pages, hardback, with Krystal Camprubiová credited as illustrator; written for young readers new to Middle-earth.
A Slovak edition also exists from Slovart (2011).
No reviews exist - all findable pages reproduce publisher copy, and the title carries too few reader votes to have a rating.
Secondary literature about Tolkien, not a work of fiction.

books.title: Three Moments of an Explosion: Stories
books.author: China Miéville
flags: Ten of the twenty-eight stories had appeared previously; first published 2015.
Includes formally experimental pieces - film-trailer texts and numbered-viewpoint fragments - alongside conventional short stories.

books.title: Blood Promise
books.author: Richelle Mead
flags: The catalogue record is titled with the series name but the annotation describes Blood Promise (the fourth novel, 2009, 503 pp.) - the record and the volume do not match, so the physical holding should be confirmed on collection.
The catalogue also holds other print editions: Domino 2014 (Katrin Mekki), Domino 2011 and Domino 2010 (both Katrin Chýlová).
Ends on a cliffhanger; preceded by Shadow Kiss and followed by Spirit Bound.
The Alchemists, a faction later central to a spin-off series, are introduced here.

prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: The Science of Discworld IV: Judgement Day
books.author: Terry Pratchett, Ian Stewart & Jack Cohen
flags: Fourth in the Science of Discworld sequence, after The Science of Discworld, The Globe and Darwin's Watch.
Published 2013; the science chapters are by Ian Stewart and Jack Cohen, the story chapters by Pratchett.

prereq.ref: (The Science of Discworld #1-3, not on the shelf)
prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: Aliens: Bug Hunt
books.author: Jonathan Maberry
flags: Aliens: Bug Hunt (Titan Books 2017), eighteen stories of which fifteen are original, and explicitly non-canon.
Contributors include Dan Abnett, Christopher Golden, Tim Lebbon, Brian Keene, Rachel Caine and Mike Resnick.
Czech: Baronet 2018, prel. Daniela Cermakova.

books.title: Zaklínačka Lota
books.author: Petra Neomillnerová
flags: The novel Psí zima (Motto) continues from where these stories end; this volume is the earlier-set material.
Publication order and series order differ - the collection was issued after the novel it precedes chronologically.
Author and reviewers place the series in the 'dirty fantasy' register - open depiction of violence and sex.
Czech original; no translation involved.

books.title: Zakon genu
books.author: Vaclav Kotrman, Leos Kysa (eds.)
flags: Czech original anthology, edited by Vaclav Kotrman and Leos Kysa, Epocha 2022; no translation involved.
Published to mark the Mendel bicentenary.

books.title: Tales from Planet Earth
books.author: Arthur C. Clarke
flags: Fourteen stories first published between 1950 and 1987, with Clarke's own commentary on each and a joint preface with Isaac Asimov.
A sampler rather than a complete collection; The Collected Stories of Arthur C. Clarke is the omnibus.
Czech: Baronet 2011, prel. Veronika Volhejnova.

books.title: K-PAX III: The Worlds of Prot
books.author: Gene Brewer
flags: Third book of Brewer's K-PAX series, following K-PAX and K-PAX II: On a Beam of Light, both of which the Czech annotation refers to by their Czech titles Svet podle Prota and Na svetelnem paprsku.
Two further volumes follow (K-PAX IV and V).
The first book was filmed in 2001; this volume was not.

prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: One Year After
books.author: William R. Forstchen
flags: A sequel; reviewers state the preceding novel (Jeden den poté / One Second After) must be read first, as this book assumes its cast and events.
A third volume, The Final Day, closes the trilogy.
Sources disagree on the elapsed time - the title says one year, the text is cited as 730 days.

prereq.ref: (Jedna vteřina poté #1, not on the shelf)
prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: From the Earth to the Moon
books.author: Jules Verne
flags: The story is completed in Around the Moon (1870); this volume ends with the projectile in flight and off course.
Many English editions are abridged nineteenth-century translations; the Czech route is translated from the French.
Czech: Dobrovsky 2016, prel. Jaroslav Horky.

books.title: 100 chyb při péči o lidi s demencí
books.author: Jutta König, Claudia Zemlin
flags: Portál 2017, translated from German by Lucie Simonová.
A carer's practical handbook, not narrative non-fiction.

books.title: Dog Training 101
books.author: Kyra Sundance
books.czTitle: 101 tipů jak vychovat poslušného a spokojeného psa
flags: Original Dog Training 101 (Quarry / Quarto 2017, about 175 pp); the catalogue's orig field carries a typo, 'Dog trainig 101'.
Same author as the bestselling 101 Dog Tricks (2007).
The genre vocabulary has no non-fiction category; recorded as testimony with form nonfiction.

books.title: 130: Hodní, zlí a oškliví
books.author: Nikkarin
flags: H.Z.A.O. stands for Hodní, zlí a oškliví.
Part of a trilogy; 130: Odysea (2009) comes before it and its plot continues here.
This is a comic, not prose.

prereq.note: The previous volume of the trilogy; its plot continues here.

books.title: Therapy Games for Teens: 150 Activities to Improve Self-Esteem, Communication, and Coping Skills
books.author: Kevin Gruzewski
flags: Original: Therapy Games for Teens, 2020, ISBN 9781647397760; the author's first book.
Marketed for recreational therapists, teachers and parents, usable with groups or individuals.
An activity manual, not narrative non-fiction.

books.title: Ala Luna
books.author: Zlatuše Marková
flags: Pointa, March 2024; print and e-book. Pointa is a Czech crowdfunding self-publishing imprint.

One Slovak retailer categorises it under sci-fi for children and young readers, while the library catalogue heading is vědecko-fantastické romány (adult novels). The audience is therefore not settled.
No reviews or ratings found for this title.

books.title: Alexandr Veliký
books.author: Karen Oganj
flags: Translated from Russian by Martin Mahdal and Marketa Adamcova; the catalogue heading is 'rusky psane romany'.
The Czech book database lists the author under the fuller name Karen L. Ohanjanyan; 'Karen Oganj' appears to be the imprint's form.
Dialog 2024. No rating, review or reader comment found; page count not established.

books.title: Apokalypsa Evropy
books.author: Zdeněk Šafář
flags: Author is a former sociology professor (b. 1938) whose earlier SF novel Evakuace appeared from the same publisher in 1996.
Reader-database average is about 1.85 out of 5.
Reader criticism singles out the choice of antagonists (homeless people, drug users, Roma).
No professional literary review was found.

books.title: Arabella of Mars
books.author: David D. Levine
flags: Book one of a trilogy; Arabella and the Battle of Venus and Arabella: The Traitor of Mars follow, and the Czech route covers only this title.
Reviewers disagree whether the Mars-set opening is a prologue or a full chapter, so the opening structure is not established here.
Marketed in English as 'Jane Austen meets Jules Verne'.

books.title: Arthur et les Minimoys
books.author: Luc Besson
flags: French original 2002; basis of the 2006 animated film Arthur and the Invisibles.
Two Czech sequels are held: Arthur v zakázaném městě (2005) and Arthur a Maltazardova pomsta (2006).
Czech reader rating around 79% on a small sample.

books.title: Besna zem
books.author: Petr Opršal
flags: Bourdon, 2026; launched as part of Velky knizni ctvrtek.
The author describes it as a post-apocalyptic novel without zombies and says the ending is positive.
Set in real north Moravian geography rather than an invented world.
The author's earlier books are Cestou z veze (2018), on leaving the Jehovah's Witnesses, and the crime novel Dokud nas krev nerozdeli (2023).
Reception evidence is author interviews, publisher promotion and reader reviews; no independent literary review was found.

books.title: Bizarní Česko
books.author: Jakub Pokorný
flags: The genre vocabulary has no nonfiction bucket, so genre is recorded as litfic with form nonfiction; the book is practical/reference nonfiction.
Pangea 2024, first edition; listings disagree on extent (312 pp paperback per the distributor, 256 pp hardcover per one retailer).

books.title: God's Grace
books.author: Bernard Malamud
flags: Malamud's eighth and last novel (1982); the Czech print route is Akropolis 1993.
Six named parts: The Flood, Cohn's Island, The Schooltree, The Virgin in the Trees, The Voice of the Prophet, God's Mercy.
A post-nuclear moral fable with talking animals; the catalogue's sci-fi keyword is loose.
Ends with the protagonist killed and the chimpanzees losing speech.

books.title: Bronzová planeta a jiná řešení
books.author: Vladimír Medek
flags: The author's own pick of his best SF stories; Millennium Publishing. Translator databases date the collection 2000, so the 2007 holding may be a reissue.
Rated about 70% on the Czech SF/fantasy database Legie, above his other fiction.
Medek (1940-2022) was primarily a translator - Garcia Marquez, Vargas Llosa, Sheckley, and with his brother Pavel the Czech Harry Potter.
Page count and contents list not established.

books.title: Byl jednou jeden úl
books.author: Karel Sládek
flags: Czech print route is UNVERIFIED on the task line (Triton 2025, no recordId); it was not checked.
The catalogue holds a 2021 printing of the same title, and Příběhy včelí královny (2025) by the same author continues the bee series.
Part of the Laskavé čtení series.

books.title: Warship
books.author: Joshua Dalzelle
flags: English original Warship (2015), book one of the Black Fleet Trilogy, self-published; the series has since expanded well past a trilogy into the Black Fleet Saga.
Czech print via Fantom Print 2016, transl. Jakub Marik.
No professional trade reviews found; reception evidence is Goodreads aggregate plus indie blogs.
Reviewers consistently report the opening is slow and heavy on exposition.

books.title: A Boy and His Bot
books.author: Daniel H. Wilson
flags: English original A Boy and His Bot (Bloomsbury Children's 2011), the author's first middle-reader; School Library Journal shelves it grades 4-7, ages nine to twelve.
Czech print via Knizni klub 2012, transl. Lumir Mikulka.
The same author's adult SF (Robopocalypse) is a different register entirely.

books.title: What Doesn't Kill Us
books.author: Scott Carney
flags: The genre vocabulary has no nonfiction bucket, so genre is recorded as testimony with form nonfiction; the book is immersive journalism with a self-experiment spine.
Foreword by Wim Hof; the English original is What Doesn't Kill Us (2017).

books.title: Breathe
books.author: Sarah Crossan
flags: English original Breathe (Greenwillow 2012), 373 pages; book one of a duology continued by Resist.
Czech print via Baronet 2013, transl. Radvan Markus.
Told in alternating chapters by three teenage narrators in first-person present.
This author's better-known books (One, Moonrise) are verse novels; this one is prose.

books.title: Storia degli italiani
books.author: Giuliano Procacci

cz.translator: Drahoslava Janderová, Bohumír Klípa, Kateřina Vinšová

flags: The genre vocabulary has no nonfiction bucket, so genre is recorded as historical with form nonfiction; the book is a survey history.
Italian original Storia degli italiani (1968); Czech NLN editions 1997, 2007 and 2010, roughly 490-500 pages.
Procacci belonged to the Italian marxist historiographical tradition, which one Czech reader names as a visible slant.

books.title: Diagnostika syndromu týraného, zneužívaného a zanedbávaného dítěte
books.author: Eva Mydlíková (ed.), Jaroslav Slaný, Mariana Kováčová
flags: 168 pages, Portál 2021, first edition, ISBN 978-80-262-1834-0; reported out of stock at some retailers.
Written by a Slovak multidisciplinary team from Trnava University and the Trnava teaching hospital.
A professional monograph, not a memoir or popular non-fiction.

books.title: Dinotopia: A Land Apart from Time
books.author: James Gurney
flags: 159 pp, illustration-led; won a Hugo for best original artwork, as did its follow-up.
Three later volumes exist: The World Beneath (1995), First Flight (1999), Journey to Chandara (2007). This one stands alone.
Czech edition Priroda 1994; the original is Turner Publishing 1992. Adapted into a TV mini-series, an animated film and video games.

books.title: Les lois naturelles de l'enfant
books.author: Céline Alvarezová
flags: French original Les lois naturelles de l'enfant; the original publication year and publisher were not confirmed by the source used, and study guides to it are catalogued from 2018 onward.
Czech edition Knizni klub 2018 in the Universum series, translated by Hana Jovanovicova.
Catalogued as a handbook, with keywords covering Montessori method, pre-school children, empathy and upbringing.

books.title: The Magdalen Girls
books.author: V.S. Alexander
flags: Kensington Books, December 2016, 304 pp.
Chapters alternate between Teagan and Nora, with some from the Mother Superior, Sister Anne.
Based on the historical Magdalene laundries in Ireland, the last of which closed in 1996.

books.title: Do pekla a zpět
books.author: Jakub Hoza
flags: Book 1 of the Strasak series; Mystery Press 2021, 376 pp, paperback.
The publisher's own copy warns of extreme violence, psychopaths and cannibals; it is pitched as a bloodier Escape from New York.
Reader scores are strong within its niche (about 84% across a few hundred ratings), but several reviewers class it as an action thriller with only a light SF colouring.
The author writes mainly dark fantasy and splatterpunk and has around eight books out.

books.title: Day of the Creepers
books.author: S.D. Stuart
flags: Third Czech volume of the series; Povstání Herobrina is the fourth. English series order runs Herobrine Rises, The Portal, Day of the Creepers, Here Be Dragons and onward.
S.D. Stuart is a pen name of Steve DeWinter; the books are unofficial fan fiction, not licensed by Mojang, and volumes are around eighty pages.
The catalogue also holds other print printings: Computer Press 2015 and 2014, both translated by Marcel Goliaš.
English series naming is inconsistent - retailers file the same volumes as Minecraft Adventures and as Herobrine's Quest.
Catalogued as a publication for children.

books.title: Matched
books.author: Ally Condieová
flags: Book one of a trilogy; Czech continuations are Dokonalý sen and Dokonalý svět, both Knižní klub.
Reading order matters: the two later Czech volumes continue this plot directly and assume this lead.

books.title: Crossed
books.author: Ally Condieová
flags: A sequel: continues Dokonalý pár and cannot be read without it; Dokonalý svět follows.
Both continuations are Knižní klub print editions, translators Martina Neradová and Klára Kučerová.

books.title: Reached
books.author: Ally Condieová
flags: A sequel that closes the trilogy; continues Dokonalý pár and Dokonalý sen and cannot be read without them.
Different Czech translator from the two earlier volumes (Klára Kučerová, Knižní klub 2013).

books.title: Došel nám čas
books.author: Barbora Walterová Benešová
flags: Brána 2018.
Czech reader rating around 68% on a small sample; no professional review found.
Publisher and page count were not independently confirmed beyond the catalogue record.

books.title: Adult Children of Emotionally Immature Parents
books.author: Lindsay C. Gibson
flags: Portal 2024, transl. Alena Svecova; original New Harbinger 2015. A follow-up, Recovering from Emotionally Immature Parents, exists.
The genre vocabulary has no non-fiction category; recorded as testimony with form nonfiction.

books.title: Dum zelenych prizraku
books.author: František Běhounek
flags: First published as Pripad profesora Hrona (1947); lightly reworked and reissued under this title in 1968.
The 1999 Milenium Publishing volume pairs it with a second novel, Akce L.
Behounek (1898-1973) was a physicist who studied radiology under Marie Curie and wrote mostly for young readers, but this title was aimed at adult readers and is regarded as his best work.
No plot synopsis beyond the publisher annotation was found in any source; character names and the nature of the 'green phantoms' were not established.

books.title: When Tomorrow Comes
books.author: Janette Okeová
flags: Part of the Canadian West cycle and later than Klid před bouří, which follows her brother; the parents' history is assumed rather than re-established.
Series identification rests on the annotation's plot (Wynn and Elizabeth's daughter Christine) rather than on a title match.

prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: Infinite
books.author: Brian Freeman
flags: Original title 'Infinite' (2021); Czech translation Jan Jirak, Euromedia/Laser 2022.
Standalone, not part of the author's Jonathan Stride crime series; the catalogue files it under 'Laser. Sci-fi' while the publisher markets it as a psychological thriller.
The author names John Fowles's 'The Magus' as the model he was working toward.

books.title: Elias mezi lidojedy
books.author: Veronika Kristofova
flags: The Czech route on this record is unverified - the task line carries cz.state 'unchecked' with no recordId, so Epocha 2022 is asserted from the publisher record only and no library holding was confirmed.
Epocha 2022, 208 pages, hardcover, illustrated by Jana Moskito; retailers file it under children's adventure/detective for the first stage of primary school.
It continues an earlier book about Elias; 'Elias a kapitan Cernovous' (Epocha 2025, 225 pages) closes the cycle.

books.title: Epištoly o elitách a lidu
books.author: Vlastimil Vondruška
flags: A loose continuation of the author's Breviář pozitivní anarchie; non-fiction, unlike the rest of his output.
The closed genre vocabulary has no non-fiction option; genre is recorded as litfic and the form field carries the truth.
No professional literary criticism could be found - all traceable reception is retailer and Databáze knih reader comment, and it is politically polarised.
Czech original, MOBA 2018, ISBN 9788024383170.

books.title: Eine feine Gesellschaft: Europas Koenigs- und Kaiserhaeuser im Spiegel ihrer Skandale
books.author: Martina Winkelhofer
flags: Ikar 2016, transl. Jiri Vodvarko; original Amalthea 2014 (304 pp), reissued by Piper 2016 as 'Skandale und Intrigen an Europas Koenigs- und Kaiserhaeusern'.
The author is a Habsburg-court historian working from archival court files.
The genre vocabulary has no non-fiction category; recorded as testimony with form nonfiction.

books.title: Finanční analýza
books.author: Adriana Knápková, Drahomíra Pavelková, Karel Šteker
flags: The genre vocabulary has no nonfiction bucket, so genre is recorded as litfic with form nonfiction; the book is practical/reference nonfiction.
Grada, Prosperita firmy series; multiple updated editions exist and the route here is the 2013 printing.

books.title: Girgal
books.author: Jan Křesadlo
flags: Subtitled 'eskapada na zpusob science fiction'; author-illustrated; Ivo Zelezny 1992, 275 pp.
Kresadlo was the pen name of the psychologist Vaclav Pinkava, who emigrated to Britain in 1968; he is better known for Mrchopevci and the Greek-hexameter SF epic Astronautilia.
Mestska knihovna v Praze has issued Girgal as a free e-book with notes on the manuscript's genesis.

books.title: H2O a poklad šíleného oka
books.author: Petr Stančík
flags: cz.state is 'unchecked' on the task line, so the Czech print route here is unverified rather than confirmed; not checked, per instruction.

Series order: 'H2O a tajná vodní mise' (Zlatá stuha 2018) precedes this title; later titles include 'H2O a pastýřové snů', 'H2O a záhada Zlaté slzy', 'H2O a zkázonosný prstenec' and 'H2O a otázka zrcadlové sfingy'.
Illustrated throughout by Galina Miklínová; an audiobook edition also exists.
The catalogue heading is 'publikace pro děti'; genre recorded as sf on the shrinking-device premise, but the register is junior adventure.

books.title: H2O a záhada Zlaté slzy
books.author: Petr Stančík
flags: Series order: 'H2O a tajná vodní mise' opens the series, followed by 'H2O a poklad šíleného oka' and 'H2O a pastýřové snů'; 'H2O a zkázonosný prstenec' and 'H2O a otázka zrcadlové sfingy' come later.
Illustrated by Galina Miklínová; the series has won Zlatá stuha and an audiobook-of-the-year award for children.
The catalogue heading is 'publikace pro děti'; genre recorded as sf on the space-travel premise, but the register is junior adventure.
The judgement rests on series-level author research plus this record's own annotation; no review of this specific title was located.

books.title: Fever
books.author: Deon Meyer
flags: Afrikaans original Koors (2016); English translation by K.L. Seegers. Roughly 500 pages.

The murder is announced in the first sentence but does not occur until past page 400, with the culprit revealed in the final pages. There is no investigation in the body of the book - Publishers Weekly's starred review calls it 'less a mystery in any sense' than a post-apocalyptic examination of the human condition, which is why this was flagged rather than rejected at the detective gate.
Multi-voice structure: most of the book is Nico's first person, interleaved with transcribed testimony from other Amanzi residents.
Sexual content was not established from sources and is not priced into the range.
The author is otherwise a crime novelist; the catalogue shelves this under thrillery (romány).

books.title: The Host
books.author: Stephenie Meyerová
flags: The catalogue also holds another print edition: Tatran 2009, Petra Klufova.
The author's first adult novel and first SF, marketed as a standalone; announced sequels (The Soul, The Seeker) were never published.
Long - the US hardcover runs about 620 pages, and some paperback printings more.
Filmed in 2013 by Andrew Niccol; most online criticism of 'The Host' refers to that film or to the unrelated 2006 Korean monster film of the same English title.

books.title: Hudba pro Anvilany
books.author: Martin Sichinger
flags: Czech original, Argo 2010, 188 pages, ISBN 978-80-257-0255-0.
The blurb ties the apparition to Father Pellegrino Ernetti, the priest who claimed to have built a device for viewing the past - real-world paranormal claim material, not examined at this exit.
Sources disagree on the name of the energy giant (EnerClad in publisher copy, EnerGaz in one write-up).
The author's better-received books are regional non-SF novels.

books.title: Le Château des étoiles / Castle in the Stars
books.author: Alex Alice
flags: This is a comic (bande dessinee), not a prose novel; the English editions are 64-page hardcovers of watercolour art.
The catalogue also holds another Czech print edition (Host 2025, Richard Podaný).
French publication is reorganised into many small albums (Le Secret de l'ether, Les Chevaliers de l'ether and onward) and runs well past the four English volumes; reading order matters.

books.title: The (Honest) Truth About Dishonesty
books.author: Dan Ariely
flags: Prah 2012, transl. Hata Komnacka; original The (Honest) Truth About Dishonesty (HarperCollins 2012). The catalogue's orig field holds the translator credit, not the original title.
The PNAS honesty-pledge paper was retracted in September 2021 over a fabricated dataset; the book itself has not been withdrawn or revised.
The genre vocabulary has no non-fiction category; recorded as testimony with form nonfiction.

books.title: Erfolgreich lernen mit ADHS: Der praktische Ratgeber fuer Eltern
books.author: Stefanie Rietzler, Fabian Grolimund
books.czTitle: Jak se úspěšně učit s ADHD
flags: Noxi 2018, transl. Tereza Tesinska; original Hogrefe/Huber 2016, expanded second edition 2023 retitled 'Erfolgreich lernen mit ADHS und ADS' (304 pp), so the Czech text follows the older version.
Companion books by the same authors exist for children (Lotte, traeumst du schon wieder?) and teenagers (Clever lernen).
The genre vocabulary has no non-fiction category; recorded as testimony with form nonfiction.

books.title: Jumper: Griffin's Story
books.author: Steven Gould
flags: English original Jumper: Griffin's Story (Tor 2007), 139 pages, written around a character created for the 2008 film.

Continuity-independent of the author's own novels Jumper, Reflex, Impulse and Exo, so it can be read without them; the catalogue annotation's claim that it follows Jumper is about the film's universe, not those books.
Czech print via Baronet 2008; no translator recorded.
A video game of the same title exists and search results conflate the two.

prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: Quarantine
books.author: Greg Egan
flags: The frame is an investigation - one professional review calls it part procedural whodunnit - but the payoff is the physics rather than a culprit; investigation-shaped subplot, flagged not vetoed.
Standalone; not part of a series. English original Quarantine (Legend 1992), about 280 pages.
Czech print via Navrat 2002, transl. Petr Kotrle.
Hard SF with sustained technical exposition; the author has since said his own better grasp of quantum computing means parts of the mechanism do not work on the book's own terms.

books.title: You're Smarter Than You Think: A Kid's Guide to Multiple Intelligences
books.author: Thomas Armstrong
flags: Original English title: You're Smarter Than You Think (Free Spirit Publishing); Czech edition Portál, ISBN 978-80-262-0019-2.
Also addressed to parents, teachers and educators running child-development programmes.
Catalogued by Portál under hry a tréninky (games and training), not psychology.

books.title: Beyond the Gathering Storm
books.author: Janette Okeová
flags: Part of the Canadian West cycle, later than its opening volume When Calls the Heart; the leads are the next generation and the earlier family history is assumed rather than re-established.
Důvěřuj zítřku, also Triton 2024, follows the sister Christine from the same family.
Series identification rests on the annotation's plot rather than on a title match - the Czech title is a loose rendering.

prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: Kognitivni trenink pro treti vek
books.author: Jana Bilkova
flags: Grada 2016, Psyche series; classified as popular-science, personal development and health. I could not source a page count or the publisher's annotation, so the content description rests on the catalogue form heading (prirucky) and the classification.
Non-fiction exercise handbook; genre recorded as testimony because the closed genre vocabulary carries no non-fiction value.

books.title: Who Can You Trust? How Technology Brought Us Together and Why It Might Drive Us Apart
books.author: Rachel Botsman
flags: Host 2018, transl. Jiri Petru; English original 2017 (Portfolio Penguin), listings differ between 2017 and 2018 editions.
Technology reporting is dated to 2017: sharing-economy platforms, blockchain, early social-credit coverage.
The genre vocabulary has no non-fiction category; recorded as testimony with form nonfiction.

books.title: Kostelík, který se radoval
books.author: Tomáš Vondrovic
flags: Czech print route is UNVERIFIED on the task line (Stanislav Juhaňák - Triton 2026, no recordId); it was not checked.
Part of the Laskavé čtení series, catalogued under náboženské příběhy and publikace pro děti.

books.title: Love Comes Softly
books.author: Janette Okeová
flags: First of eight in the Love Comes Softly series; the Czech cycle carries the same name.
The series was adapted into a run of television films, which is a different work from the novel.
Author writes explicitly inspirational fiction; the publisher's Czech line is Stanislav Juhanak - Triton.

books.title: Cold People
books.author: Tom Rob Smith
flags: English original Cold People (Scribner 2023), 368 pages; Czech print via Euromedia 2024, transl. Ivan Rycovsky.

Kirkus describes the opening as a single concrete thread - a family reaching Antarctica by supertanker and caught in an offshore logjam against the deadline - and the aliens are never seen or heard in the book.
The story spans a generation, so later sections follow the engineered children; the POV count was not established.
Kirkus flags one character's attraction to an engineered person as awkwardly handled; the sexual-content axis was not examined at this exit.
The author is best known for the crime novel Child 44.

books.title: Literatur und Politik
books.author: Joseph P. Strelka

cz.publisher: Brno : Centrum pro studium demokracie a kultury, 2001
cz.translator: Lucie Topoľská, překlad veršů Radek Malý

flags: The genre vocabulary has no nonfiction bucket, so genre is recorded as litfic with form nonfiction; the book is practical/reference nonfiction.
German original Literatur und Politik; Czech subtitle 'Pohledy z literarnevedne perspektivy', CDK Brno 2001, translated by Lucy Topolska with verse translations by Radek Maly.
Appears to be out of print; only secondary-market listings were found.

books.title: DK Eyewitness Top 10 London
books.author: Roger Williams
flags: The genre vocabulary has no nonfiction bucket, so genre is recorded as litfic with form nonfiction; the book is practical/reference nonfiction.
Other Czech Top 10 London editions are recorded: Ikar 2002, Euromedia Group 2006 and a Lingea Top 10 - Londyn 2023.
Guidebook content is dated by definition; the route here is a 2011 printing.

books.title: Lovci
books.author: František Kotleta
flags: 304 pages, first edition Epocha 2015, volume 40 of the Fantastická Epocha series.
A Czech audiobook exists, read by Josef Kaluža.
Standalone; not part of the author's Underground or SPAD sequences.

books.title: Magician: Master
books.author: Raymond E. Feist
flags: This is the second half of Feist's single 1982 novel Magician, which the Czech edition splits in two; Čarodějův učeň is the first half and this book continues its plot directly with the same lead, so it cannot be read on its own.
The catalogue holds a second print edition (Wales 2011).
Followed in the same saga by Silverthorn and A Darkness at Sethanon.

books.title: Magical Child
books.author: Joseph Chilton Pearce
flags: Malvern 2019, transl. Katerina Ctiborova; original Magical Child (1977). A follow-up volume, Magical Child Matures (1985), exists.
Reviewers report a chapter on child psychics and telepathy; the occult question was not examined at this exit.
The genre vocabulary has no non-fiction category; recorded as testimony with form nonfiction.

books.title: Malevil
books.author: Robert Merle
flags: Won the John W. Campbell Memorial Award for best SF novel in 1974; French original 1972.

The catalogue heading on this record includes 'kompaktni disky' and 'mluvene slovo', so the 2017 Kristian entertainment holding is likely the 10-hour Czech audiobook (dir. Jan Jiran, read by Martin Mysicka and a large cast) rather than a print run.
The catalogue also holds another print edition: 2013, trans. Vera Dvorakova.
A 1981 French film adaptation exists; Merle disowned it and asked for his name off the credits, and its plot departs almost entirely from the novel.

books.title: Malirky
books.author: Denisa Proskova
flags: 224 pages, hardcover, ISBN 9788024296098; Universum is the Euromedia imprint, not a series.
The subtitle varies between listings: '48 jmen, ktera nezapadla v dejinach malovanych muzi' and '48 jmen, ktera nezapadla v dejinach umeni psanych muzi'.
Illustrated by the author; reader reviews note the absence of reproductions of the painters' works.
Sources disagree on the historical span - the publisher says Renaissance onward, one review says from the 7th century BC.

books.title: Fabulous Figures and Cool Calculations
books.author: Colin Stuart
flags: English original Fabulous Figures and Cool Calculations (Colin Stuart, 2018, 80 pages), catalogued as juvenile literature under mathematics and experiments.
Czech edition Euromedia 2018 in the Pikola series, translated by Marek Chvatal.
Catalogued as a popular-educational publication for children.

books.title: Mechanické rybičky
books.author: Vojtěch Otčenášek
flags: Comics/illustrated format, written and illustrated by the same person; the catalogue keywords are 'ekologie', 'komiksy', 'sci-fi'. Recorded here as a novella because 'comic' is not one of the available form values.
The catalogue author string is malformed - 'a ilustroval] Vojtech Otcenasek' - so the credit is author-and-illustrator, one person.
Edika (Brno) 2012. No rating, annotation beyond the catalogue's, or reader reviews found in the Czech book databases.

books.title: Metalstory: Příběh kovu
books.author: Michael Newchop
flags: Issued by Klika in 2022 in two parts, 'Metalstory - Příběh kovu 1' (about 300 pp) and 'Metalstory - Příběh kovu 2' (about 372 pp); the split is reported to have been a binding constraint rather than a structural choice, so the two together are one work.
An e-book edition (2023) collects it at about 365 pp.
'Michael Newchop' is a pseudonym and is also the name of the protagonist - a deliberate metafictional move noted by reviewers. No review in an established literary outlet was located.
The cover was generated by AI.

books.title: Migot: Z krance Grenlandii
books.author: Ilona Wisniewska
flags: Absynt 2024, Prokleti reporteri series, 224 pp., translated from Polish by Michaela Benesova; Polish original Migot: Z kranca Grenlandii (2022).

The author's first book translated into Czech; the northern series continues with Bile. Ledova vyspa Spicberku (2014), Hen. Na severu Norska (2016) and Led. Z gronskeho ostrova (2018), which are separate reportages and not sequels - none is needed to read this one.
Non-fiction reportage; genre recorded as testimony, which is the nearest value in the closed vocabulary.

books.title: Mijamoto Musasi
books.author: Jakub Zeman
flags: The Czech route on this record is unverified - cz.state is 'unchecked' with no recordId, so Epocha 2024 is asserted from the publisher record only.

The catalogue annotation on this record describes the continuation (after the duel with Sasaki Kojiro), while the year given is 2024; the 2024 Epocha title is 'Mijamoto Musasi: Pribeh psany mecem' (232 pages, illustrated by Jiri Straka), and a review site reports 'Mijamoto Musasi: Dva mece' (Epocha 2026). The record may conflate the two.
A Czech audiobook of the 2024 book exists; it was named one of the ten best books of Svet knihy Praha 2025.
The author teaches swordsmanship in his own dojo and received an honorary award from the Japanese ambassador in 2025.

books.title: The Adult ADHD and Anxiety Workbook: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Skills to Manage Stress, Find Focus, and Reclaim Your Life
books.author: J. Russell Ramsay
flags: Original: New Harbinger, ISBN 9781648482434, with a contribution by Ari Tuckman.
Positioned for use alone or alongside professional treatment; includes online worksheets in the original edition.
A clinical exercise workbook, not a memoir.

books.title: Můj bratr Mesiáš
books.author: Martin Vopěnka
flags: Mladá fronta 2017, hardcover, with an e-book edition; promoted internationally via CzechLit.
The narrative spans 2096 to 2168, the later strand set in a Greek settlement near Olympus.
Reader rating 65% from 39 ratings on databazeknih; no review in an established Czech literary outlet (iLiteratura, Host, Tvar, A2) was located.
Whether any miracle or rite is staged on the page was not established from a source; reader accounts mention none.

books.title: Návrat Krále Šumavy
books.author: Karel Osoha, Ondřej Kavalír, Vojtěch Mašek
flags: This is a comics adaptation of David Jan Žák's biographical novel Návrat Krále Šumavy (2012), a different book from the prose original.
The comics trilogy runs Na čáře (2018), Agent-chodec (2019), Opona se zatahuje (2020); the catalogue record covers the Labyrint editions and holds the 2018 and 2019 printings as well.
The prose original by David Jan Žák is a separate available route to the same story.

books.title: Heimkehr auf die Kamelien-Insel
books.author: Tabea Bachová
flags: Third book of the Kamelien-Insel saga; preceded by Die Kamelien-Insel and Die Frauen der Kamelien-Insel. Not readable independently - the heroine's inheritance of the island and her marriage happen in the earlier books.
German original Bastei Luebbe 2019; the heroine is Sylvia in the German text.
Marketed as a feel-good saga about a Breton nursery garden.
Reception is reader reviews only; the recurring criticism is that this volume is almost too dramatic.

books.title: Návštěvníci
books.author: Ota Hofman
flags: Originally serialised in the children's magazine Pionyr, and the book is more condensed than the 1983 television series it accompanies; the relationship is parallel rather than the series adapting the book.
Albatros editions 1985, 1994 and 2008 exist (the catalogue records the publisher as 'Albatos', an evident typo); some printings include stills from the series.
The catalogue keywords are 'roman' and 'sci-fi'; Hofman wrote chiefly for children.

books.title: De nachtdienst
books.author: Nova Lee Maier
flags: Published in the Netherlands in 2021 as De nachtdienst under the author's own name, Esther Verhoef; Nova Lee Maier is the pseudonym used for foreign editions.
177 short chapters plus an epilogue, spanning about a year with occasional flashbacks; the 2024 Dutch paperback runs 384 pp.
No English edition found.

books.title: Nebojte se zmen
books.author: Helena Mackova
flags: Grada, Psychologie pro kazdeho series; the publisher page carries a March 2025 timestamp consistent with a 2025 edition, but I did not source an ISBN or page count.

The author's professional training, as listed on her own site and course pages, includes systemic, family and business constellations, NLP, EMDR and Ericksonian hypnosis. Whether any such practice is set out as an exercise for the reader inside this book is not established and is the specific thing to check before proposing it.
Non-fiction self-help; genre recorded as testimony because the closed genre vocabulary carries no non-fiction value.

books.title: Drawing and Painting the Undead
books.author: Keith Thompson
flags: Original title 'Drawing and Painting the Undead'; Czech translation Tomas Suchanek, Zoner Press 2009, 128 pages, paperback.
Part of Zoner's 'Naucte se kreslit' instructional series, which is what the catalogue's series field records.
Instructional art book, not fiction - the genre label is the subject matter, not a narrative genre.
The same author wrote '50 Robots to Draw and Paint' and '50 Fantasy Vehicles to Draw and Paint'.

books.title: Neviditelní zloději
books.author: Irena Zítková
flags: An anthology, not a single-author work: Irena Zitkova is the compiler. The full title is 'Neviditelni zlodeji: vedeckofantasticke povidky mladych ceskych autoru' and it takes its name from Ludmila Freiova's story.
Contributors include Zdenek Volny, Eduard Martin, Ladislav Szalai and Ludmila Freiova; illustrated by Theodor Rotrekl.
The catalogue record carries no annotation. The publisher is recorded as 'Albatos', an evident typo for Albatros.
Historically the first of a wave of Czech SF anthologies - about ten had appeared by 1990, including Zelezo prichazi z hvezd and Lide ze souhvezdi Lva.

books.title: Neviditelní
books.author: Vlastimil Vondruška
flags: Czech original, no translation involved; MOBA 2021, also issued as an e-book.
Publisher annotations differ between retailers on details including the heroine's name and the interval since the Reset - the catalogue record used here says Klaud and forty years.
The author is much better known for historical crime fiction; this is one of his contemporary-politics works, alongside Kronika zániku Evropy.
Reader reception is strongly polarised along political lines rather than literary ones.

books.title: Neztrať mapu k mému srdci
books.author: Hana Repová
flags: Translated from Slovak by Lucie Vesela; published in the Dobrovsky 'Red' romance imprint, 2023, with a 2023 e-book edition.
Not part of the author's Soukrome problemy series.
Reader ratings on Czech book databases are high (roughly 83-89 percent), all from readers of the romance imprint's own audience.

books.title: Never Split the Difference: Negotiating As If Your Life Depended On It
books.author: Chris Voss a Tahl Raz
books.czTitle: Nikdy nedělej kompromis, aneb, Vyjednávej tak, jako by ti šlo o život
flags: Czech translation by Eva Nevrla, Jan Melvil Publishing 2016, in the publisher's Zadna velka veda line.
Co-written with Tahl Raz.
Framed explicitly as an alternative to Getting to Yes by Roger Fisher and William Ury.

Non-fiction; genre recorded as testimony because the closed genre vocabulary carries no non-fiction value, and there is no narrative opening structure to establish, which is why confidence is medium rather than high.

A recorded criticism worth knowing: hostage negotiation is one-shot and power-asymmetric, so how far the method generalises to repeated commercial dealings is contested; I did not find a scholarly test of that claim.

books.title: Nolens volens, czyli, Chcac nie chcac
books.author: Zuzanna Kisielewska
flags: Polish original Nolens volens, czyli chcac nie chcac by Zuzanna Kisielewska.
A Slovak edition exists as Tajomstva slavnych vyrokov (2022), localised with regional content.
The Czech Labyrint / Raketa edition details come from the catalogue record and were not independently confirmed by the source used.
Catalogued as a popular-educational publication for children.

books.title: Nová Gaia
books.author: Samuel Isaacson

cz.translator: sazba a grafická úprava: Jakub Drkal

flags: Second volume of the 'Entram' gamebook trilogy; the first is 'Astronaut' (original title 'The Altimer', 2023, transl. Jakub Drkal).
Gamebook form - numbered branching passages with character and combat rules; 'novel' is the nearest value in the form vocabulary and is recorded for that reason only.
The task line's cz.translator field carries a typesetting credit rather than a translator name; copied verbatim as instructed.
Author listed as British, born 1984; the original English title of this volume was not located.

books.title: Odmaturuj! z literatury
books.author: Vlastimil Čech, Olga Mužíková, Pavel Slepička
flags: The genre vocabulary has no nonfiction bucket, so genre is recorded as litfic with form nonfiction; the book is practical/reference nonfiction.
Didaktis, Odmaturuj! series; several similarly titled volumes exist, including Odmaturuj z literatury 2 and Odmaturuj z literatury - Testy, so the catalogue record fixes which one this is.

books.title: Operace Slunce
books.author: Václav Šorel
flags: Prose reworking of the author's 2008/09 comics serial from the magazine ABC, in the same line as his Vzpoura mozku and Galaxia; some editions reproduce panels from the comic.
XYZ 2019, 184 pp, hardback; an e-book edition exists.
The catalogue genre/form heading includes 'publikace pro deti'.

books.title: Pán blesků
books.author: Michaela Hánová
flags: Volume one of a planned cycle, subtitled Neuvěřitelný příběh vynálezce Nikoly Tesly; further volumes are announced rather than published.
Czech original from a small Moravian publisher (MaHa, Hustopeče, 2025); no ISBN, plot summary, reviews or author biography could be found online.
Page count disagrees between sources - the library record says 207 pages, the retailer listing 240.
The publisher's own genre label is historicky sci-fi roman; the catalogue files it under biographical, historical and science-fiction novels at once.

books.title: The New World of Mr Tompkins
books.author: George Gamow, Russell Stannard
books.czTitle: Pan Tompkins stále v říši divů
flags: A 1999 revision by Russell Stannard of George Gamow's Mr Tompkins in Paperback (1965), itself a merger of two earlier Tompkins books; Stannard added new material on modern particle physics and cosmology, so roughly a third is not Gamow.
Popular science with a fictional frame rather than a novel; the catalogue files it under sci-fi.
Illustrated, in Gamow's own simple style; the Czech edition is Aurora 2001.

books.title: Hellhole
books.author: Brian Herbert, Kevin J. Anderson
flags: First of the Hellhole trilogy, followed by Hellhole: Awakening and Hellhole: Inferno; this volume ends on a cliffhanger.
An original setting by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson, unconnected to Dune.
The Czech record is Baronet 2014, translated by Dana Chodilová; no later Czech volume was on the task line.

books.title: How to Write a Story, Grades 1-3
books.author: Jo Ellen Moore, Marilyn Evans, Leslie Sorg
flags: Original Evan-Moor 'How to Write a Story, Grades 1-3' (2001, 96 pp), a reproducible teacher resource; a Grades 4-6 volume exists.
Czech edition Safran 2014, transl. Katerina Safrankova; catalogue form headings are 'pracovni listy / prirucky / ucebni texty'.
The genre vocabulary has no non-fiction category; recorded as testimony with form nonfiction.

books.title: Song for the Unraveling of the World
books.author: Brian Evenson
flags: 22 stories; the collection won the 2019 Shirley Jackson Award for a single-author collection and a Ray Bradbury Prize, per publisher-supplied copy - the catalogue annotation's World Fantasy Award claim is not what the sources report.
English original Coffee House Press 2019, 240 pages; Czech edition Gnom! 2023, translated by Jakub Nemecek, in the Horla series.
Reviewers report recurring Evenson devices: the possibly-mad earnest narrator, empty threatening buildings, withheld reveals.

books.title: Pod znamenim pulmesice
books.author: Luděk Frýbort
flags: Subtitled 'Pribehy z Evropy pod vladou islamu'; 448 pages; the author's eighth book.
Ludek Frybort (1933-2019) was a Czech exile author; retailers shelve the book as Czech SF.
Several parallel storylines in different countries; the opening structure was not established.
No professional literary review was found; all reception evidence is reader databases.

books.title: Strange Skies Over East Berlin
books.author: Jeff Loveness
flags: Originally a four-issue BOOM! Studios comics miniseries (2019-20), written by Jeff Loveness with art by Lisandro Estherren; the Czech Comics Centrum volume is the collected edition.
Comics form; the read log contains no comics, so there is no calibration for it.
ComicBookRoundUp aggregate is 8.0 across the four issues; reader reception is mixed.
The espionage plot is investigation-shaped but the payoff is not the identity of a culprit.

books.title: The Betrayal: The True Story of My Brush with Death in the World of Narcos and Launderers
books.author: Robert Mazur
flags: Non-fiction memoir, not a novel: the catalogue heading 'americke romany / thrillery (romany)' is wrong.

A sequel to Mazur's earlier memoir The Infiltrator (filmed 2016); readable without it, since the earlier operation is recapped, and no taste filter attaches to the predecessor, so nothing is inherited.
Part of the spine is identifying who betrayed the operation - an investigation-shaped thread in an otherwise non-detective book.
The genre vocabulary has no non-fiction category; recorded as testimony with form nonfiction.

books.title: Poslední Follower
books.author: vytvořili Martin Petro & Viktor Asimov
flags: This is a comics album (catalogue heading: sci-fi komiksy), not prose; script by Viktor Asimov and Martin Petro, art by Juraj Nasticky.
Slovak original, Czech translation by Lenka Vanousova; continues from Posledni Follower 1 (Formulator 2021), which collects a prologue and five episodes plus a bonus.
The catalogue also holds another print edition: Formulator 2022, Lenka Vanousova.
Expl0ited, Duklock and Moon are fictionalised versions of real Slovak and Czech YouTubers, which is the marketing hook.

books.title: Rasskazy o rodine
books.author: Dmitry Glukhovsky
flags: Russian original Rasskazy o rodine, first AST edition 2010, reissued 2022; Czech edition Knizni klub 2017, translated by Pavla Boskova.
Same author as Metro 2033.
Only marketing copy and individual reader reviews were found; no professional criticism.

books.title: Here Be Dragons
books.author: S.D. Stuart
flags: Fourth Czech volume of the series, after Dobrodružství Minecraftu; it continues the same three children and the same pursuit.

The Czech title translates the English Herobrine Rises, which is the series' first volume, but the annotation matches the fourth English episode, Here Be Dragons - the identification rests on the plot, not the title.
S.D. Stuart is a pen name of Steve DeWinter; unofficial fan fiction, not licensed by Mojang.
The catalogue also holds another Computer Press 2015 printing, same translator.
Catalogued as a publication for children.

books.title: Not Your Mother's Rules: The New Secrets for Dating
books.author: Ellen Feinová a Sherrie Schneiderová
books.czTitle: Pravidla, kterými se vaše matka neřídila
flags: The genre vocabulary has no nonfiction bucket, so genre is recorded as litfic with form nonfiction; the book is practical/reference nonfiction.
English original Not Your Mother's Rules: The New Secrets for Dating (2013), a sequel to The Rules (1995).
The series has drawn sustained criticism for being prescriptive and anti-feminist, and for having no research base.

books.title: Rules of War
books.author: Iain Gale
flags: Original title 'Rules of War' (HarperCollins). Second Jack Steel novel: 'Man of Honour' precedes it, 'Brothers in Arms' follows.
Czech translation Jana Simonova, Talpress 2012.

An undercover traitor-hunt is a substantial strand, but the satisfaction is not whodunnit - it is a soldier's mission behind the lines - so the detective bar was examined and not applied. Flagged, not vetoed.
The publisher pitches it explicitly at Bernard Cornwell and Patrick O'Brian readers; reader reviews split on whether the prose carries it.

prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: Transforming the Living Legacy of Trauma: A Workbook for Survivors and Therapists
books.author: Janina Fisher
flags: Portal 2023, transl. Linda Bartosova; original PESI 2021. The catalogue's orig title is slightly wrong - it is 'Transforming the Living Legacy of Trauma'.
Includes internal-family-systems parts-work worksheets; a companion psychoeducational flip chart exists.
The genre vocabulary has no non-fiction category; recorded as testimony with form nonfiction.

books.title: The Ferryman
books.author: Justin Cronin
flags: Standalone; unconnected to the author's The Passage trilogy. English original The Ferryman (Ballantine 2023), about 560 pages.
Czech print via Euromedia 2024, transl. Jakub Marek.
Reception is split on the resolution: Kirkus starred it, while the New York Times and the Washington Post were lukewarm and one review called the ending lackluster after a long setup.
The plot is mystery-shaped - the lead is investigating what Prospera actually is - but the answer is a premise, not a culprit.

books.title: The Great Cities in History
books.author: John Julius Norwich (ed.)
flags: Slovart 2019, transl. Miroslav Kolac and Jiri Matas; original Thames & Hudson 2009, paperback reissue 2016.
Multi-author anthology; contributors named in publisher copy include Jan Morris, Simon Schama, Orlando Figes and A. N. Wilson.
The genre vocabulary has no non-fiction category; recorded as testimony with form nonfiction.

books.title: Přímo tady, mezi vámi
books.author: Kateřina Müllerová
flags: Czech original, Pointa 2025; Pointa publishes by reader crowdfunding, and no professional review had appeared at the time of checking.
One reader review is essentially the whole reception; described as a quick, bite-sized read.
Format: alternating diary narrators plus a transcript, with the interrogated character's name redacted throughout.

books.title: The Positivity Effect: Simple CBT Skills to Transform Anxiety and Negativity into Optimism and Hope
books.author: Dan Tomasulo
books.czTitle: Proměňte úzkost v naději pomocí KBT
flags: Original: New Harbinger, ISBN 9781648481116, with a foreword by Lisa Miller.
By the author of Learned Hopefulness.
A self-help exercise workbook, not a memoir or narrative non-fiction.

books.title: Promeny Kafkovy Prahy
books.author: Václav Kotrman, Jaroslav Kříž (eds.)
flags: Compiled for Epocha by Vaclav Kotrman and Jaroslav Kriz for the centenary of Kafka's death (1924-2024).

A Czech audiobook exists (Audioteka/Epocha), read by Jitka Mouckova and Jan Maxian.

Coverage found is blogs and reader ratings, including an acknowledged review copy - no established Czech literary-critical review surfaced.

books.title: První pomoc

Several unrelated Czech handbooks share the title Prvni pomoc.
Vigue is credited as editor of the original illustrated volume, not as a single author.

books.title: Psychiatricke minimum

Non-fiction explainer; genre recorded as testimony because the closed genre vocabulary carries no non-fiction value.

books.author: Marc-Uwe Kling
flags: German original 2017; a sequel, QualityLand 2.0, exists.
A second storyline runs in parallel with Peter's: a presidential election between the android candidate John of Us and a demagogue named Conrad Cook.
The text is interleaved with satirical fake advertisements, news items and quizzes rather than running as continuous narrative.
One reviewer content-rating puts sex at 2/5 (sexual themes, nudity, masturbation) and violence at 3/5.
Surnames in the setting derive from a parent's profession, which is the source of much of the crude naming humour.

books.title: The Language of Emotions: What Your Feelings Are Trying to Tell You

flags: A revised and updated English edition exists (2020s) with a new chapter on anxiety and more on trauma resolution; the Czech Noxi 2016 translation is of the earlier text.

books.title: Reinkarnace – Opožděný návrat

flags: Full title Reinkarnace – Opožděný návrat; 208 pages, Brána 2013, first edition, hardcover.

Around 16 reader ratings and no professional review found. Readers describe it as a historical reincarnation novel rather than hard science fiction, though the catalogue heading is vědecko-fantastické romány.
The premise is a dead person's soul taking over another body rather than classical rebirth.

books.title: Remo
