Reviewers: three alternating storylines, one that never joins the others; slow until the aliens appear.
No Czech print edition in either library.

enText.why: Plain modern prose with some technical mining vocabulary.

books.title: Enclave
books.author: Ann Aguirre
flags: Razorland #1; later volumes continue the story.
No Czech print edition found; read in English.

enText.why: Short sentences in present-tense first person; plain modern YA prose.

books.title: Ender in Exile
books.author: Orson Scott Card
flags: Chronologically sits between Ender's Game and Speaker for the Dead; written 2008, best read after Ender's Game.
Reviewers: first fifty pages are letters and discussion; structure is episodic.
No Czech print edition in either library.

enText.why: Card's plain, clear modern prose.

books.title: Eon
books.author: Greg Bear
flags: Series: The Way #1; Eternity is #2 and carries the story on.
Reviewers disagree on the Stone's arrival year (1999 vs 2005).

enText.why: Hard-SF vocabulary and long political and mathematical passages, but standard prose.

books.title: Furies of Calderon
books.author: Jim Butcher
flags: Codex Alera #1; the next volumes continue the story.
Opens with several POVs in the first chapters.
No Czech print edition found; read in English.

enText.why: Standard genre prose, but several POVs and many invented terms for furies, ranks and peoples.

books.title: Gregor the Overlander
books.author: Suzanne Collins
flags: Series (Underland Chronicles, five books); later books grow more violent.
Czech print 2018 Fragment, translator Zdik Dusek.

books.title: Shadow and Bone
books.author: Leigh Bardugo
flags: Grisha #1; later volumes continue the story and depend on this one.
Czech edition by Fragment 2021.

books.title: Half Way Home
books.author: Hugh Howey
flags: Self-published 2012, re-released 2019. Reviewers disagree on the number of survivors.

enText.why: Plain first-person young-adult prose.

books.title: Hallucinations
books.author: Oliver Sacks
flags: Reviews: most recommended of the author's books; some find the brain descriptions heavy.
No Czech print edition in either library.

enText.why: Clear anecdotes, but dense medical terminology and long sentences.

books.title: The Hero of Ages
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: Third of the original Mistborn trilogy; depends on the two before it. No Czech print edition in the catalogue.

enText.why: Plain modern prose; the metal-magic terms are explained in use.

books.title: Starship Troopers
books.author: Robert A. Heinlein
flags: Opens in the middle of a raid, then flashes back to Rico's school years.
Classroom lecture sections carry much of the philosophy.

enText.why: Plain first-person 1950s prose, but long expository speeches and military jargon.

books.title: Incarceron
books.author: Catherine Fisher
flags: Book 1 of Incarceron; Sapphique is the follow-on and the story is not complete without it.
The book alternates between Finn (inside) and Claudia (outside).
Czech edition Knizni klub 2011, translator Petra Diestlerova.

books.title: Iron Gold
books.author: Pierce Brown
flags: Fourth in Red Rising Saga: Red Rising, Golden Son, Morning Star, Iron Gold, Dark Age, Light Bringer, Red God; Morning Star (not in the log) comes first.
First multi-viewpoint book in the series: Darrow, Lyria, Ephraim, Lysander.
No Czech print edition in either library.

enText.why: Fast prose but heavy invented slang and four threads.

books.title: Isles of the Emberdark
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: Continues the novella Sixth of the Dusk, set five years later, and ties into Tress of the Emerald Sea and the wider Cosmere; reviewers say it is not the best entry point for newcomers.
Opening is two threads with invented terms; read the premise first.

enText.why: Plain modern prose, but heavy invented Cosmere jargon and two threads to track.

prereq.ref: (Sixth of the Dusk, novella, not on the shelf)
prereq.note: Set five years after the novella; marketed as standalone.

books.title: Calamity
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: Third and last of the Reckoners trilogy; read the two before it first. No Czech print edition in the catalogue.

enText.why: Plain, fast first-person modern prose with a youthful voice and short chapters.

books.title: Assassin's Apprentice
books.author: Robin Hobb
flags: Farseer Trilogy #1; Royal Assassin and Assassin's Quest continue the same story and depend on this book.
No Czech print edition found; read in English.

enText.why: Plain but dense first-person retrospective prose with long paragraphs and little dialogue; invented names are easy, reading is slow rather than the vocabulary hard.

books.title: Blood Red Road
books.author: Moira Young
flags: Dustlands #1; later volumes continue the story.
Czech print is at the second library (Roznov), CooBoo 2013.
Written in a phonetic dialect without quotation marks.

books.title: Light Bringer
books.author: Pierce Brown
flags: Sixth in Red Rising Saga, followed by Red God; read Morning Star and earlier volumes first.
Four viewpoints, per one reader.
No Czech print edition in either library.

enText.why: Fast but heavy invented slang and military terms.

books.title: The Choice
books.author: Edith Eger
flags: Roughly half memoir, half therapy case studies (sections Prison, Escape, Freedom, Healing).
Czech edition Prah 2019, translator Karina Mateju.

books.title: Oathbringer
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: Third of the Stormlight Archive; depends on the two before it. Unfinished saga. No Czech print edition in the catalogue.

enText.why: Plain modern prose, but very long, with many invented terms (spren, highstorms, Vorin customs) and a big cast.

books.title: The Moon Is a Harsh Mistress
books.author: Robert A. Heinlein
flags: Narration imitates Loonie speech and drops articles; it takes some pages to get used to.
Standalone.

enText.why: Narrator's invented Loonie dialect drops articles and bends grammar, plus political and economic argument; readable after a few chapters.

books.title: Mission of Gravity
books.author: Hal Clement
flags: Series: Mesklin #1; Star Light follows.
Corrected figure: author said polar gravity should be about 250g, not 700g.

enText.why: 1953 prose with technical exposition, short and direct.

books.title: Escape
books.author: Carolyn Jessop
flags: Written with Laura Palmer.
Czech edition Ikar 2009, translator Alexandra Fraisova.
The sect is the FLDS; the marriage is plural and religious rather than legal.

books.title: Musicophilia: Tales of Music and the Brain
books.author: Oliver Sacks
flags: Seven-part collection of case histories; no Czech print edition in either library.

enText.why: Erudite, medical vocabulary, long sentences, but clear anecdotes.

books.title: The Heavenly Man
books.author: Brother Yun
flags: Written with Paul Hattaway.
Authenticity of the miracle accounts (74-day fast, prison escape) is publicly disputed, with co-author and supporters defending it.
No Czech print edition held; read in English.

enText.why: Simple, direct, first-person prose with short sentences and religious vocabulary; Chinese names and places are the main load.

books.title: Unbroken
books.author: Laura Hillenbrand
flags: Biography by a researcher, not Zamperini's own memoir.
Czech edition Jota 2015, translator Jaroslava Novotna.
Closes with the post-war years and a religious conversion; faith is a thread late in the book.

books.title: Nor Crystal Tears
books.author: Alan Dean Foster
flags: Series: Humanx Commonwealth #9 by publication; reviewers say it stands alone.

enText.why: Plain adventure prose.

books.title: Notes from the Burning Age
books.author: Claire North
flags: Stand-alone novel. Some roles use invented pronouns.

enText.why: Dense literary prose with invented terms and unusual pronoun use.

books.title: Steelheart
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: First of the Reckoners trilogy (Steelheart, Firefight, Calamity). Has a mystery-shaped thread about the Epics' weaknesses; flagged, not a veto. No Czech print edition in the catalogue.

enText.why: Plain, fast first-person modern prose with a youthful voice and short chapters.

books.title: A Fire Upon the Deep
books.author: Vernor Vinge
flags: Zones of Thought #1, Hugo winner 1993. The prologue is dense with invented terms; a plot summary beforehand helps. A Deepness in the Sky and The Children of the Sky are related books.

enText.why: Dense invented terms in the prologue, then clear readable prose; Usenet-style posts in places.

books.title: Firefight
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: Second of the Reckoners trilogy; read Steelheart first. No Czech print edition in the catalogue.

enText.why: Plain, fast first-person modern prose with a youthful voice and short chapters.

books.title: On Basilisk Station
books.author: David Weber
flags: Series (Honor Harrington, 14 plus books).
Reviewers complain about expository tactical passages.

enText.why: Standard genre prose with long technical exposition and naval vocabulary.

books.title: Sheepfarmer's Daughter
books.author: Elizabeth Moon
flags: Series (Deed of Paksenarrion, three books); the story continues in the next books.
Contains an attempted rape by an officer, off-page, with its aftermath shown.

books.title: Pastwatch: The Redemption of Christopher Columbus
books.author: Orson Scott Card
flags: Standalone; two alternating storylines, one future, one Columbus's life.
Reviews: argued as a defence of colonialism; sacrifice among the Mexica is the stated alternative; not confirmed whether staged on the page.
No Czech print edition in either library.

enText.why: Plain prose, but historical detail and long moral argument.

books.title: Pathfinder
books.author: Orson Scott Card
flags: First of the Pathfinder trilogy: Pathfinder, Ruins (2012), Visitors (2014).
Reviewers: long, time-paradox dialogue divides readers; two alternating storylines, the second shorter.
No Czech print edition in either library.

enText.why: Clear prose, but long time-paradox dialogues are hard to follow.

books.title: Planetfall
books.author: Emma Newman
flags: Series: Planetfall #1; After Atlas is a companion novel; reviewers advise reading this first.

enText.why: Plain first-person present-tense prose.

books.title: The Alloy of Law
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: First of the second Mistborn era (Wax and Wayne), followed by Shadows of Self, The Bands of Mourning and The Lost Metal. Has an investigation-shaped thread (the gang's kidnappings); the satisfaction is adventure, not whodunnit. No Czech print edition in the catalogue.

enText.why: Plain prose, but one major character speaks in heavy cockney-style slang that a non-native reader may find hard to parse.

books.title: The Last Colony
books.author: John Scalzi
flags: Old Man's War #3; the leads come from Old Man's War and The Ghost Brigades. Zoe's Tale retells the same events from another viewpoint.

enText.why: Plain first-person prose, snappy dialogue.

books.title: The Well of Ascension
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: Second of the original Mistborn trilogy; read The Final Empire first. No Czech print edition in the catalogue.

enText.why: Plain modern prose; the metal-magic terms are explained in use.

books.title: Prey: Immigration, Islam, and the Erosion of Women's Rights
books.author: Ayaan Hirsi Ali
flags: Non-fiction polemic rather than memoir; reviewers dispute its use of anecdotes and statistics. Genre field set to testimony as the closest allowed value.

enText.why: Journalistic prose with statistics and legal terms.

books.title: Alive: The Story of the Andes Survivors
books.author: Piers Paul Read
flags: Chapters also follow the families searching and the plane's passengers before the crash.
No Czech print edition held; read in English.

enText.why: Clean 1970s journalistic prose with long sentences, some Spanish names and place names and mountaineering and aviation terms; large cast to follow.

books.title: Promise of Blood
books.author: Brian McClellan
flags: Powder Mage #1; later volumes continue the story.
Adamat's thread is an investigation (mystery-shaped subplot, not the main plot).
Opening drops into an ongoing coup; reading a short premise summary first helps.

books.title: The Curse of Chalion
books.author: Lois McMaster Bujold
flags: Series (World of the Five Gods): other books follow different characters in the same world.
Possible occult veto: a death-magic rite is staged; judged as an invented system, doubt noted in why.

enText.why: Elegant standard fantasy prose with some theological vocabulary and court intrigue.

books.title: Deathworld
books.author: Harry Harrison
flags: Series: Deathworld #1; #2 The Ethical Engineer and #3 The Horse Barbarians follow with little link to Pyrrus.
Hugo-nominated; serialised in Astounding 1960.

enText.why: Short 1960 pulp prose, direct, with some dated dialogue.

books.title: The Rithmatist
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: Standalone so far; planned sequels unpublished. Has an investigation at its centre (kidnappings of students). No Czech print edition in the catalogue.

enText.why: Plain, young-adult prose.

books.title: Rhythm of War
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: Fourth of the Stormlight Archive; depends on the three before it. Unfinished saga. No Czech print edition in the catalogue.

enText.why: Plain modern prose, but very long, with many invented terms (spren, highstorms, Vorin customs) and a big cast.

books.title: Scion
books.author: James Islington
flags: Goodreads lists it as Scion #1, but series status is disputed and one reviewer says it reads like a prologue. Published 1 September 2026; about 240 pages.

enText.why: Short, fast thriller prose.

books.title: Seeing Voices
books.author: Oliver Sacks
flags: Reviews: the most scholarly of the author's books; endnotes take up a large part of the volume.
No Czech print edition in either library.

enText.why: Dense linguistics terminology and scholarly history, plus long endnotes.

books.title: Semiosis
books.author: Sue Burke
flags: Series: Semiosis #1; Interference follows and Usurpation is #3.
Seven sections, one POV per generation (Kara Reviews, Space Cat Press).

enText.why: Plain, accessible prose; the plant's narration is readable.

books.title: Touching the Void
books.author: Joe Simpson
flags: Czech edition Jota 2001; translator not given.
After the rope is cut the book alternates between Simpson and Yates.

books.title: Orphanage
books.author: Robert Buettner
flags: Series: Jason Wander #1; read first, #2 Orphan's Destiny follows.
Chapter one is a frame set near the end of the story and the rest is flashback journal (SFFWorld).

enText.why: Plain first-person military prose, short chapters.

books.title: Words of Radiance
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: Second of the Stormlight Archive; read The Way of Kings first. Unfinished saga. No Czech print edition in the catalogue.

enText.why: Plain modern prose, but very long, with many invented terms (spren, highstorms, Vorin customs) and a big cast.

books.title: Slow Bullets
books.author: Alastair Reynolds
flags: Novella, about 200 pages in print.

enText.why: Clean prose with some invented military and tech terms.

books.title: The Sunlit Man
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: Written as a Cosmere standalone but Nomad's identity and backstory come from the Stormlight Archive; reviewers say it relies on prior Cosmere knowledge.
Opening is shape two (mid-action, backstory only alluded to): read a plot summary of the premise first.
Czech print Talpress 2025 held at the second library.

books.title: Sufficiently Advanced Magic
books.author: Andrew Rowe
flags: Arcane Ascension #1; later volumes continue the story.
Game-like magic system with long explanations.
No Czech print edition found; read in English.

enText.why: Plain modern prose; the difficulty is the volume of game-style terminology, not the sentences.

books.title: Terminal World
books.author: Alastair Reynolds
flags: Stand-alone novel.

enText.why: Reynolds's long sentences and invented terms, but straightforward adventure plotting.

books.title: The Black Cloud
books.author: Fred Hoyle
flags: Standalone novel.

enText.why: 1950s British prose with heavy scientific vocabulary and dialogue.

books.title: The Girl of Fire and Thorns
books.author: Rae Carson
flags: Fire and Thorns #1; the story continues in later volumes.
Faith and scripture are a constant thread.
No Czech print edition found; read in English.

enText.why: Clear YA first-person prose; Spanish-flavoured names and some religious vocabulary but simple sentences.

books.title: The Girl with Seven Names
books.author: Hyeonseo Lee
flags: Written with David John; the author has seven names across the book.
No Czech print edition held; read in English.

enText.why: Plain, brisk modern prose with short sentences; reviewers call it a light, easy read and finished it in two days.

books.title: The Lives of Tao
books.author: Wesley Chu
flags: Series: Tao #1; The Deaths of Tao follows.

enText.why: Light modern comic prose.

books.title: The Peace War
books.author: Vernor Vinge
flags: Across Realtime #1; Marooned in Realtime follows a different lead (Wil Brierson) and contains a murder-mystery strand. Brierson is not the lead here.

enText.why: Plain, brisk 1980s SF prose.

books.title: The Praxis
books.author: Walter Jon Williams
flags: Series: Dread Empire's Fall #1; The Sundering and Conventions of War follow.

enText.why: Standard space-opera prose with many invented species and ranks.

books.title: The Red: First Light
books.author: Linda Nagata
flags: Series: The Red #1; Going Dark and Trials follow.
Three loosely linked parts.

enText.why: Military jargon and technical terms, otherwise standard prose.

books.title: The Strength of the Few
books.author: James Islington
flags: Hierarchy #2; read The Will of the Many first, since this picks up directly and assumes the lead and world. Three first-person present-tense viewpoints, marked by a symbol at each chapter start. Next volume is The Justice of One; the series is planned as four books.

enText.why: Long, dense epic-fantasy prose with invented terms and three narrators to track.

books.title: The Sudden Appearance of Hope
books.author: Claire North
flags: Stand-alone novel; the author also publishes as Catherine Webb and Kate Griffin.

enText.why: Stylised, long-sentence literary prose.

books.title: The Sword of Kaigen
books.author: M. L. Wang
flags: Theonite #1 in the catalogue; billed as a standalone with a cliffhanger.
Heavy content warnings: war, abuse, rape, suicide.
No Czech print edition found; read in English.

enText.why: Fluent, emotional prose with Japanese-inspired terms and a large cast; about 680 pages, but sentences are not dense.

books.title: Tomorrow, When the War Began
books.author: John Marsden
flags: Tomorrow #1; the series continues for several volumes.
No Czech print edition found; read in English.

enText.why: Plain conversational first-person prose with some Australian slang.

books.title: Trading in Danger
books.author: Elizabeth Moon
flags: Series (Vatta's War, five books).
C-low exit: occult status unexamined.

enText.why: Plain, brisk modern prose; ship and trade jargon is explained as it comes.

books.title: Traitor's Blade
books.author: Sébastien de Castell
flags: Greatcoats #1; later volumes continue the story.
Backstory contains a who-killed-the-king question, not the main plot.
No Czech print edition found; read in English.

enText.why: Witty first-person-leaning prose with swordplay vocabulary and invented titles; sentences are moderately long but followable.

books.title: The Warrior's Apprentice
books.author: Lois McMaster Bujold
flags: Chronologically after Shards of Honor and Barrayar, but works as a start; Czech order numbers it first.
Bothari's backstory includes past sexual violence, mentioned and not staged.

enText.why: Clear, witty modern prose; some invented military and planetary terms.

prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: Uglies
books.author: Scott Westerfeld
flags: Series: Uglies #1; Pretties, Specials and Extras follow.

enText.why: Plain YA prose with some invented slang.

books.title: Unsouled
books.author: Will Wight
flags: Cradle #1; short at 294 pages; the series continues for many volumes.
No Czech print edition found; read in English.

enText.why: Plain modern genre prose, short sentences, a handful of invented terms explained as they come.

books.title: Escape from Camp 14
books.author: Blaine Harden
flags: In 2015 Shin admitted parts were untrue; author Blaine Harden added a foreword (he places Shin in camps 14 and 18, two escapes, and a larger role in his mother's and brother's fate). Later printings carry the foreword.
Czech edition Ikar 2013, translator Kamila Weiserova.
Written by a journalist from interviews, not first-person.

books.title: The Hiding Place
books.author: Corrie ten Boom
flags: Written with John and Elizabeth Sherrill, about 25 years after events.
A young-reader abridgement exists; this is the full original.
Heavy religious framing; reviews call it hagiographic.

enText.why: Plain, conversational 1970s prose by professional collaborators; short sentences, little archaic or technical vocabulary beyond a few Dutch and German terms.

books.title: The Forever War
books.author: Joe Haldeman
flags: A direct continuation, Forever Free (1999), exists; Forever Peace is only a thematic companion.
Contains a mandatory-sex military culture and later compulsory homosexuality as a world feature.

enText.why: Direct, spare prose with military slang and physics terms.

books.title: The Sparrow
books.author: Mary Doria Russell
flags: Series (The Sparrow, two books); the story continues in Children of God.
Content: sexual violence and trauma are central to the later timeline.

enText.why: Literary, character-driven prose with linguistic and Jesuit terms, split across two timelines.

books.title: Warbreaker
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: Standalone Cosmere novel; no required reading order.

books.title: Educated
books.author: Tara Westover
flags: Parts of the account are disputed by members of the author's family; names are altered.
Czech edition Mlada fronta 2022, translator Olga Bartova.

books.title: Defiant
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: Fourth and last book of the Skyward series; depends on Skyward, Starsight and Cytonic and on the connected Skyward Flight novellas.

books.title: The Memory of Earth
books.author: Orson Scott Card
flags: First of the five-book Homecoming saga (Memory of Earth, then The Call of Earth and three more); structured on the opening chapters of 1 Nephi.
Reviewers mention sacred-lake and barbed-ring rites in the city.
No Czech print edition in either library.

enText.why: Plain prose, but many invented names and a slow, dialogue-heavy build.

books.title: Wind and Truth
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: Fifth of the Stormlight Archive; closes the first arc, the saga continues in a second half not yet published. Includes a romance between Renarin and Rlain (AV Club, Beyond Hogwarts); not checked against the text. No Czech print edition in the catalogue.

enText.why: Plain modern prose, but very long, with many invented terms (spren, highstorms, Vorin customs) and a big cast.

books.title: Nomad
books.author: Ayaan Hirsi Ali
books.czTitle: Z područí islámu: otázka integrace muslimů do západní společnosti
flags: Original is Nomad: From Islam to America (2010). Companion to her memoir Infidel, which is not required.

enText.why: Clear essayistic prose with political and religious terms.

books.title: The Collapsing Empire
books.author: John Scalzi
flags: The Interdependency #1; the story is unfinished at its end and continues in The Consuming Fire and The Last Emperox.

enText.why: Plain contemporary prose, heavy swearing and banter.

books.title: The Testing
books.author: Joelle Charbonneau
flags: The Testing #1; later volumes continue the story.
Czech edition by Fragment 2016.

books.title: The Mind's Eye
books.author: Oliver Sacks
flags: Collection of case essays with a memoir thread; no Czech print edition in either library.

enText.why: Erudite vocabulary and long sentences but clear stories.

books.title: The Lost Metal
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: Fourth of the Wax and Wayne books; depends on The Alloy of Law, Shadows of Self and The Bands of Mourning, to be read first. No Czech print edition in the catalogue.

enText.why: Plain prose; heavy slang from a main supporting character and the cosmic-level setting add some load.

prereq.ref: (Mistborn: Wax and Wayne #2-3, not on the shelf)
prereq.note: Earlier volume of this series, not held in Czech print or not screened yet (audit 2026-10-29).

books.title: Blood Brothers
books.author: Elias Chacour
flags: Co-written with David Hazard, 1984.

enText.why: Clear narrative prose co-written for general readers; some Arabic and Middle East political history terms.

books.title: Bruchko
books.author: Bruce Olson
flags: First published 1973; its accuracy and Olson's methods are disputed by some anthropologists and defended by others.
Exited at C-low with one source.

enText.why: Plain, fast first-person narrative with simple vocabulary.

books.title: Captive in Iran
books.author: Maryam Rostampour, Marziyeh Amirizadeh
flags: Co-written with John R. Perry, 2013.

enText.why: Plain co-written narrative prose with a few Persian terms.

books.title: Cry, the Beloved Country
books.author: Alan Paton
flags: Published 1948; South Africa on the eve of apartheid.
A murder trial runs through the plot but the culprit is not in question.

enText.why: Simple vocabulary but a stately, biblical rhythm, 1940s South African terms, and some long lyrical passages.

books.title: Dawn of Wonder
books.author: Jonathan Renshaw
flags: Series: The Wakening, with further books; only this first one assessed.
Reviewers mention a long training-academy section after the first chapters.

enText.why: Standard epic-fantasy prose, described by reviewers as rich and poetic, with some long sentences and invented place names.

books.title: Delta-v
books.author: Daniel Suarez
flags: Neither library holds a Czech print edition.
Catalogued as the first of a series.

enText.why: Technical thriller prose with engineering and legal terms but short chapters.

books.title: Elder Race
books.author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
flags: Novella; two alternating viewpoints, Lyn in third person past and Nyr in first person present.
Neither library holds a Czech print edition.

enText.why: Short novella with plain prose; both narrative voices are easy to follow.

books.title: End of the Spear
books.author: Steve Saint
flags: Continues the story begun in Through Gates of Splendor (Elisabeth Elliot, 1957).
The film of the same title does not follow the book closely.

enText.why: Plain narrative prose with Waodani names and terms and shifts between times.

prereq.ref: (Through Gates of Splendor, Elisabeth Elliot, not on the shelf)
prereq.note: Continues the same events from the other side; readable alone.

books.title: Endurance: Shackleton's Incredible Voyage
books.author: Alfred Lansing
books.czTitle: Endurance: Neuvěřitelné putování Shackletonovy Královské transantarktické expedice
flags: Published 1959; based on diaries and interviews with survivors.
The Czech title in the catalogue is a translation; neither library holds a print copy.

enText.why: Clear, matter-of-fact 1950s prose, with some nautical and polar terms and mixed units.

books.title: I Dared to Call Him Father
books.author: Bilquis Sheikh
flags: Published 1978, co-written with Richard Schneider.
Exited at C-low with one source; not verified past the summary.

enText.why: Plain, direct 1970s memoir prose, short chapters, little jargon beyond Urdu and Islamic terms.

books.title: In the Presence of My Enemies
books.author: Gracia Burnham
flags: Written with Dean Merrill, 2003; updated edition adds an epilogue.

enText.why: Plain, direct narrative co-written for a general audience.

books.title: Contact
books.author: Carl Sagan
flags: Standalone.
Neither library holds a Czech print edition.
Adapted as the 1997 film.

enText.why: Clear 1980s prose with long expository passages on science and religion.

books.title: Theft of Swords
books.author: Michael J. Sullivan
flags: Omnibus of The Crown Conspiracy and Avempartha, books 1 and 2 of Riyria Revelations.
Neither library holds a Czech print edition.

enText.why: Plain modern adventure prose with short chapters and lots of dialogue.

books.title: Tress of the Emerald Sea
books.author: Brandon Sanderson
flags: Standalone Cosmere novel narrated by Hoid; no prior Cosmere reading needed.
Neither library holds a Czech print edition.

enText.why: Light, humorous modern prose with a playful narrator.

books.title: Lost Moon (Apollo 13)
books.author: Jim Lovell, Jeffrey Kluger
flags: Published 1994 as Lost Moon, later reissued as Apollo 13; Lovell co-wrote with Jeffrey Kluger.

enText.why: Readable narrative prose, but heavy NASA acronyms and technical dialogue, which reviewers say the book explains.

books.title: Sea of Rust
books.author: C. Robert Cargill
flags: Standalone; later books continue the setting.
Neither library holds a Czech print edition.
Flashback chapters alternate with the present-day quest.

enText.why: Plain, voice-driven prose with short sentences.

books.title: Born a Crime
books.author: Trevor Noah

sweeps.label: Non-SF category screen — testimony, allegory, parable
sweeps.why: The genre screen only ever covered SF/F, but the log's highest non-fiction score (Seeking Allah 91) and two of its safest reads (Little Prince 82, Animal Farm 78) sit outside it. 'Genre is otherwise open' was recorded as a fact and never acted on.
lessons: The broad category terms are near-useless as-is: 'vzpominky' and 'biografie' are ~2000 records each of mostly Czech celebrity and local-history memoir. Targeted theme AND queries (Ujgur, islam autobiografie, Severni Korea) yielded far more per request than any full-category pull.

'svedectvi' (521) is dominated by Holocaust and communism testimony. That is the Anne Frank 40 form, which failed outright — so a hit in this category is NOT automatically a Qureshi 91 analogue. What earns is examined truth plus another group's lived experience, and contemporary contested subjects (Xinjiang, apostasy, North Korea) match it far better than the historical canon does.

sweeps.lesson: The category is NOT the safe-category goldmine its size suggested. 2176 records reduce to a thin canonical seam: the single largest holding is Ladislav Beran with 34 police-procedural collections (hard detective filter), and the bulk of the rest is Czech humour, literary mainstream and local memoir. The target-author pass found nearly everything of value; the frequency pass added little. For a category this large and this heterogeneous, screen by known-good author names first, and only then by imprint.

sweeps.name: children's crossover — the literatura pro děti a mládež heading, in full

The two standing category rejects on that shelf (axis:life-phase, 2026-08-26) were deliberately looked past for this pass and still stand for the default queue.
sweeps.method: Full enumeration of the heading (68 pages at pageSize=100, pageNumber is 1-based - page 0 returns HTTP 500). Each record's MARC detailTableRows were parsed for author (field 100-a), genre/form index terms, keywords, page count and annotation. A mechanical filter dropped 4,398 records - format (leporela, komiksy, manga, workbooks, encyclopedias, audio, poetry) 2,376; under 100 pages 1,142; no page count 501; detective or romance genre terms 379 - leaving 2,381 records and 1,094 authors, of which 1,053 had never been considered. That author list was then name-reviewed in full.
sweeps.lesson: The heading sweep alone would have missed a third of the crossover canon, because the library files the best of it as adult prose: Nekonečný příběh, Momo, Sofiin svět, Alenka, Medvídek Pú, Zlodějka knih, Robinson Crusoe, Huckleberry Finn and Chlapec v pruhovaném pyžamu are all absent from literatura pro děti a mládež and were recovered only by named queries afterwards. So for THIS category the two methods are complements, not alternatives - the heading finds what is shelved as children's, the named-canon pass finds what outgrew the shelf. Second finding: the page-count filter is the cheapest picture-book discriminator there is (1,142 of 6,779 records are under 100 pages) but it also cuts exactly at Little Prince length, so anything short and canonical has to be recovered by name.

sweeps.scope: Terry Pratchett, complete author holding; assessed for the Discworld series only
sweeps.lesson: Talpress publishes Discworld as TWO-NOVEL OMNIBUS volumes, and MARC 245 puts the second novel in $b, so the catalogue `name` is one title while `subtitle` is a DIFFERENT novel. Nine records collapse eighteen novels this way. A title-string join therefore misses half the series - 'Mali bohove' and 'Tezke melodicno' are reachable only as the second half of a volume named after another book. Read `subtitle` and `Udaje o edici` (which carries both numbers, e.g. '13, 14') before concluding a volume is not held. Second: the CZECH series numbering is NOT the English canon numbering - the catalogue calls Going Postal 30 where the English series calls it 33, because the Czech run excludes the Tiffany books and the Science of Discworld volumes. Use the catalogue's own number and name the English title beside it. Third, a method error worth more than a book: detailTableRows is a list of {columns:[{content:label},{content:htmlValue}]}, NOT {label,value} - a parser using label/value keys silently returns nothing at all, which is what happened on the first pass here and made 52 records look annotation-free when 40 of them carry a real Czech plot summary.
sweeps.ruledOut: Occult, 7 titles plus a sub-series row: Discworld's witches are drawn from documented English folk witchcraft and their rites are performed on the page, failing both the source and the depiction test - the Harry Potter 51 objection, and the reader's own words were that magic drawn from real-world historical witchcraft is not fine. Detective, 4 titles: the Watch volumes whose engine is a murder or theft inquiry, one confirmed by the library's own annotation ('Kdo vrazdi neskodne starce? ... vystopovat vraha'). Opening, 2 titles: The Light Fantastic and the 1+2 omnibus, both requiring the volume already abandoned at 30. Category, 1 row: the board game, the Cabell biography, the encyclopedia foreword, the cat humour book and Science of Discworld IV are not novels.
sweeps.notYetSwept: The Pratchett NON-Discworld holdings, deliberately out of scope because the request was the Discworld series: 'Dlouha zeme' and 'Dlouha valka' (with Stephen Baxter, Talpress 2013 and 2014) are the strongest untouched axis match in this author - one declared premise, stepping sideways into an unbounded chain of parallel Earths, with the annotation describing consequences being worked out; 'Filuta' (Dodger, 2016); and the story collections 'Jednim tahem pera' (Kniha Zlin 2024) and 'Mrknuti obrazovky' (2021). NOT held by this library and so unreachable: Zlodej casu, Nocni hlidka, Buch!, Neviditelni akademici, Posledni hrdina, and the remaining Tiffany Aching volumes.

coverage._readme: Answer to 'what is not screened yet', measured 2026-08-26 rather than estimated. Recomputed by re-running the union count in the sweeps' scratch pulls; if that data is gone, re-pull the swept slices listed in sweeps[].

composition._method: Stratified sample of 1500 records across 15 pages spread over the full 1093-page enumeration (1.4%), tallied on each record's own `fond` and `type` fields.

Caveat: ruska 47 and polska 66 look implausibly low for this region, so older Soviet-era translations are probably catalogued under different headings - do not read those two totals as complete.
